The "Schiller Salon" and "Goethe Salon" are so named with good reason: in the lobby you can see the old tabletop upon which both men left their mark back in the 18C. The service is also on point. Host Matthias Gugeler is the welcoming face of the restaurant: his efficient front-of-house team serves with a personal touch and helps you find your way around the wine list. The lunch menu proposes quality fare at a somewhat lower price.

name: Schwarz Gourmet
review: At the start of the German Wine Route, this sleek and elegant little restaurant housed in a charming red sandstone building has been run by Manfred Schwarz since March 2017. The Waiblingen-born chef has already proven his culinary credentials at the Schwarzberg – Lammershof by Schwarz in Löhrbach (Birkenau), at schwarz Das Restaurant in Heidelberg, and at the Schwarzer Hahn in Deidesheim. A doyen of fine dining, the chef has not lost his touch. He is able to combine individual components into sincere and clearly structured dishes that abound with clean flavours and steer clear of excessive creativity. Top-notch ingredients are used as a matter of course, as becomes clear upon sampling his prime beef or Breton scallops, among other dishes.

name: Keidenzeller Hof
review: Set in a small village, this former farmhouse has been given a facelift that retains much of its original character while introducing modern details. Wood and stone features blend tastefully and elegantly to create a chic, stylish interior. Chef Martin Grimmer proposes a creative seasonal set menu (pre-order vegetarian version). His cooking involves original ideas and subtle combinations – even the appetisers hit the mark. He enthusiastically talks you through the dishes, which his charming wife then serves. On Saturdays you can come for the"Gourmet Lunch" and on Sundays for a roast. The barn is an ideal space for parties.

name: Zeik
review: Maurizio Oster is the name of the owner and chef of this modern, minimalist, almost purist-style little restaurant. His north German roots are also reflected in his cuisine – the region takes centre stage. Select seasonal produce is put to work imaginatively. The chef likes to play with different techniques and create interesting contrasts of flavours. The result is a well-conceived, coherently structured set menu, which also comes in a vegetarian version. The chef has a real penchant for fermenting, preserving and making vinegar. In addition to wine, there is a non-alcoholic accompaniment to the menu – here they only offer drinks they produce themselves. The staff are very friendly and well trained – the cooks also bring out the food and talk you through the dishes.

name: Carmelo Greco
review: Are you a fan of Italian cuisine and the Italian lifestyle? Then follow the small signs and you will find this somewhat tucked-away restaurant easily enough. Born in Sicily and raised in Piedmont, Carmelo Greco also feels a culinary connection to his homeland. A glass of spumante to start off with, bread baked in-house, professional service replete with Italian charm... "la dolce vita" in Frankfurt! There are two set menus (one of which is vegetarian), from which you can also order à la carte. Here, creativity, finesse and impeccable technical skill are brought to bear on selected ingredients. The modern and elegant interior is done out in elegant shades of grey and gold, with chic ceiling lights and a shimmering silver bar that catches the eye as soon as you enter. Outside, the pretty terrace beckons.

Even after all these years, 5 is still bang on trend. This is primarily down to Alexander Dinter's modern cuisine. Since 2018, he has been the creative force at the helm, successfully incorporating his own original ideas into his seasonally inspired set menu. The location near the Schlossgarten, in what was Stuttgart's first ever railway station, is also unique. A laid-back urban vibe combined with an elegant lounge decor makes for a special atmosphere, which persists as you move from the stylish bar on the ground floor to the "casual fine dining" restaurant on the first floor. Here, guests sit on chic, individually designed chairs at bare tables to enjoy the excellent food and service, which includes expert wine recommendations. The parking garages in the immediate vicinity are convenient for those coming by car.

name: Genießer Stube
review: Daniel Raub represents the third generation at the helm of this dedicated family-run business. After working for Dieter Müller at Schloss Lerbach in Bergisch Gladbach, among others, he took over the kitchen of the Genießer Stube in Landhaus Biewald in 2011. In a tastefully decorated dining area complete with conservatory, diners take their seats at tables decked with beautiful settings. The professional service comes courtesy of a charming front-of-house team. At the stove, Daniel Raub gives pride of place to the ingredients, steering clear of gimmickry and harnessing his own individual style. At lunchtime there is the "Tassenmenü", and in the evening you can look forward to the "Feinschmeckermenü". You may prefer to order à la carte. The wine list is also worth a look. Incidentally, the second restaurant, Zur Tränke, has relocated to the newly constructed hotel building.

name: Schwarzer Hahn
review: Here at the Hotel Deidesheimer Hof, the dedication of the Hahn family is plain to see, especially when it comes to the restaurant. In this beautiful historical building, the contrast between the old cross vault and the modern table settings and colourful decor hits the mark perfectly. The international cuisine is prepared using select ingredients. The Saumagen (stuffed pig's stomach) – a regional specialty - must not be missing. Stefan Neugebauer and Felix Jarzina are responsible for the excellent cuisine. A word to the wise: The friendly and experienced front-of-house team will be happy to talk you through the regional wines, which are available on tap.

name: Bachofer
review: Did you know that this fine house on the market square is the second oldest in Waiblingen? It dates back to 1647 and was once a pharmacy. But beyond the historical setting, this restaurant is firmly rooted in the present, from the furnishings to the cuisine. Chef-patron Bernd Bachofer has a style all of his own, which clearly – and very coherently – draws inspiration from the great cuisines of Asia. First-rate produce is used to conjure up creative, meticulously prepared dishes brimming with unexpected taste sensations. There is also a vegetarian menu. To top it all off: elegant decor comprising a counter affording the best view of the kitchen and a professional, well-rehearsed and very friendly front-of-house team. Reasonably priced lunch. Tip: There are stylish guestrooms above the restaurant.

name: Zur Krone
review: From Miami to Neupotz. In October 2015, after many years of restaurant experience in the US, Kerstin and Faycal Bettioui took over the traditional Krone here in the tranquil Palatinate town of Neupotz (which happens to be her home town) and turned it into a chic and contemporary space. Little wonder it has been so well received, as in addition to the attentive, friendly and well-drilled service, diners are particularly impressed by Faycal Bettioui's pleasingly straightforward cuisine. For his modern eight-course tasting menu, this Moroccan-born chef draws on select international and regional produce that is in keeping with the seasons. The wine pairings by the glass are excellent – an alcohol-free version is also available. Tip: you can park next to the building or on the main street.

name: The O'ROOM
review: Absolutely in keeping with the spirit of the times: "casual fine dining" under the same roof as the Marc O'Polo Strandcasino store. The head chef in this stylish little restaurant is André Kähler, whose modern, boldly creative set menu is full of beautifully expressive flavours. Each course comes with a small card explaining the inspiration behind it. The chic interior design and pleasantly relaxed and professional service team are also noteworthy. Tip: The small delicatessen corner where, for example, the wines served can be bought to enjoy at home. For a more casual alternative, head to O'ne, which proposes modern cuisine that puts the spotlight on local produce.

name: Christian & Friends, Tastekitchen
review: First things first: be sure to make a reservation, because this place is in high demand! This isn't surprising given the fantastic set menu that Christian Steska proposes in this smart townhouse situated in the beautiful old town. The restaurant comprises both Christian & Friends and the adjoining wine bar Bordeaux & Friends with its distinctive wine rack – it has an excellent selection of wines with many top labels offered at fair prices. The open kitchen sends out modern dishes that are built on classical foundations and have a real depth of flavour. The chef has a penchant for regional produce, including caviar – Fulda boasts two sustainable sturgeon farms with their own caviar production. The pleasant atmosphere is down in no small part to the cordial service.

name: Friedrich Franz
review: This wonderfully luxurious and elegant gourmet restaurant is situated in the side wing of the exclusive Grand Hotel Heiligendamm in a wonderful location by the Baltic Sea – also known as the "white city by the sea". The sense of opulence extends to the cuisine, which comes courtesy of head chef Ronny Siewert, who hails from Nienburg (Saale). He and his kitchen team turn out delicately flavoured and elaborately detailed dishes that draw on only the most exclusive produce. The front-of-house team, led by Berlin-born Norman Rex, also knows how to impress: guests can look forward to attentive and elegant service, as well as expert advice when it comes to wine. Try to get a table by the window for a view of the sea!

name: Nagaya
review: Yoshizumi Nagaya's cuisine really is something special. In a thoughtful, bold and meticulous fashion, he fuses elements of Japanese and western cuisine. During his training in Osaka, Toshiro Kandagawa taught him traditional Japanese cookery, while he learned his innovative approach from Takada Hasho in Gifu. Drawing on both of these experiences, he has developed his own distinctive style. Excellent ingredients are a matter of honour for this chef, from the Wagyu beef to sushi and sashimi. As well as fine wines, there is a splendid selection of sake. Furthermore, the front-of-house team is attentive and professional, and the decor is very modern, stylish and upscale.

name: Richard
review: Yes, this really is it, but don’t be put off by the somewhat lacklustre exterior. Inside the former Köpenicker Hof, built in 1900, the fine interior boasts an ornate ceiling, designer lighting and artwork (the owner Hans Richard is also a painter). It provides the perfect setting for the excellent, artful and reasonably priced set menu.

name: Merkles Restaurant
review: It is safe to say that Thomas Merkle made the right decision when, together with his wife, he took over his parents' business and continued the tradition of hospitality that has been cultivated here for over 30 years. Born in Endingen, he proudly showcases his affinity with his homeland by opting for regional ingredients, but also introduces a dash of cosmopolitan flair to his well-thought-out dishes with flavours from far-flung lands. Top-quality produce, accomplished service and an appealing array of wines by the glass. The chef and his kitchen team also like to show their faces in the dining room – contact with the guests is important to them! This historical vicarage with a sleek and elegant interior makes for a pleasant setting. Good to know: Delicious treats in the form of house-made sauces, oils, and salts are also available to take away with you.

name: Seestern
review: Here you can take in the view of the lake as you enjoy Michelin-starred cuisine – it doesn't get much better than this! Diners in Hotel Lago's fine dining restaurant are bowled over not only by the view but also by the interior with its warm wood and maritime colours, high-quality furnishings and elegant Nordic design. In summer, guests can make the most of the terrace with its lounge and small sandy beach; in winter, the wood-burning stove makes for a cosy atmosphere. The focus lies squarely on the modern dishes devised by Klaus Buderath, who was responsible for the Michelin-starred cuisine at Landgasthof Adler in Rammingen and also won a star for Lago's restaurant. Born in Böblingen, his elaborate cooking is technically demanding, extremely precise and full of finesse, with an impressively clear sense of direction. Top tip: Try the non-alcoholic drink pairings!

name: Setzkasten
review: A gourmet restaurant in a supermarket? This fine dining concept is quite a novelty – to be experienced in the basement of the Crown, one of the largest food markets in Europe. It is not only the location that is worth mentioning: in addition to the smart decor and the partially open kitchen, the dedicated kitchen team serves up creative, modern cuisine made using select produce. The refined and pared-down dishes demonstrate a beautiful balance of flavours. All the wines on the list are also available by the glass. Top tip: If you really want to see what the kitchen can do, make a reservation at the chef's table. Those who arrive by car can make use of the Crown's multi-storey car park.

name: Agata's
review: For those who like their food modern and creative, this interesting mix of European and Asian cuisine is just the ticket. Everything served here is made from excellent produce and is brimming with finesse and original ideas. What's more, the chic and at the same time inviting atmosphere makes this a really nice place to be. Modern design, earthy tones, floral decorations... the entire interior is tasteful and of high quality! You are in the capable hands of proprietor Agata Reul – who hails from Poland – and her charming team, who also have plenty of savvy advice to guide you in your choice of wine.

name: Oettinger's Restaurant
review: The motto of this restaurant with a pleasing country-house style and relaxed, friendly and accomplished service translates roughly to "classy but not stuffy". This is a family business that has a tradition stretching back over 150 years. Michael Oettinger, who runs the place together with his brother Martin, has been at the helm here since 2005, after stints working at Burgrestaurant Staufeneck in Salach and Louis C. Jakob in Hamburg, among other places. The cuisine, which gives a nod to modern culinary traditions, is prepared using ingredients of the highest quality. Two set menus are proposed: "TeamWork" and "AbInsBeet", which is the vegetarian option. The restaurant's signature dish is its bouillabaisse, which can be added to the set menu. For overnight stays, Hotel Hirsch has lovely, comfortable guestrooms.

name: Cordo
review: Everything about this place is highly sophisticated yet unpretentious. First, there is the trendy but cosy decor with its original decorative details and gorgeous place settings on polished natural wooden tables. The charming and relaxed service follows suit; head chef Yannic Stockhausen also makes his rounds through the restaurant. His cuisine is in perfect keeping with this modern setting: an inventive set menu (also available in vegetarian form) that creates culinary harmony by contrasting flavours and textures. He takes a resource-saving and environmentally friendly approach to cooking, making a point of using ingredients that are produced locally. The extensive wine list features an interesting selection of natural and organic wines, which are also offered as pairings.

name: Kucher's Gourmet
review: For more than 30 years, the Kucher family has run this place with passion and dedication, constantly investing in and improving their establishment. Now it is the turn of son Florian Kucher and daughter Stefanie Becker, who have breathed new life into this gourmet restaurant. In tasteful and elegant surroundings, diners are treated to a choice of two set menus: first, "Florian's Klassik Menü", and second, the "Modern Art Menü". Subtle contrasts and intense flavours characterise the cuisine of this young chef. The wine list is certainly one of the best in Germany – with about 1 700 labels, it is a veritable El Dorado for wine lovers! Guestrooms are available in both the main and new buildings.

name: Hirsch
review: Drawing guests from near and far, this cosy restaurant has been a veritable institution in the Swabian Jura for many years. Your friendly hosts are Gerd and Silke Windhösel, who ply their trade with a great sense of dedication. At the helm in the kitchen, Gerd Windhösel makes a point of using only the freshest ingredients when creating his dishes. The chef-patron also prefers to source everything from the surrounding area – from the local pasture-raised lamb to the Seckach trout and even the saffron. This is classic seasonal cuisine of the highest standard; it demonstrates a pleasingly straightforward style that steers clear of unnecessary frills while maintaining a sense of tradition. There is a choice of different set menus, including a vegetarian one, as well as a range of "Hirsch classics" available à la carte.

name: Philipp
review: Heike and Michael Philipp have been dedicated to keeping their guests happy for more than 20 years. After training together in the legendary Schweizer Stuben in Wertheim-Bettingen, they both upped sticks and moved to the Franconian region he grew up in. It isn't just the locals who appreciate chef Michael Philipp's modern take on classic cuisine, which also draws on Mediterranean and Asian influences. When it comes to wine, you can rely entirely on the recommendations of your extremely charming and accomplished hostess and sommelier, Heike Philipp. The setting is also worth a mention: this stylish and cosy restaurant exudes historical flair, housed as it is in a picture-perfect 400-year-old Renaissance palace in the middle of a picturesque winegrowing village.

name: maiBeck
review: Jan Cornelius Maier and Tobias Becker (or "maiBeck" for short) really hit the spot with their reasonably priced fine dining cuisine. Their location in the old town between the cathedral and the Rhine isn't too bad either. The atmosphere is appealingly unpretentious, as are the two proprietors, who prove themselves to be extremely genial hosts. Perfectly in keeping with the friendly, informal look and feel of the place, the cuisine is similarly uncomplicated. Pared-down dishes are delivered without any frills; the chefs rely instead on top-quality produce to create intense, punchy flavours. Regional influences also feature heavily on the modern menu. Good to know: most of the dishes are available in smaller portions. Head out to the lovely terrace to sit and watch the tourists go by.

name: Haubentaucher
review: The fabulous lakeside location and wonderful terrace are certainly part of the appeal here, but this restaurant has plenty more to recommend it. Owner and head chef Alois Neuschmid (who also earned a Michelin star years ago with Lois, his previous venture here) makes sure of that. His modern cooking focuses entirely on the excellent ingredients. While at lunchtime you choose dishes from the blackboard, in the evening there is a surprise menu, alongside which judicious wine pairings are recommended. The outstanding food is complemented by an enjoyably unpretentious atmosphere and very friendly service – with the chef himself also occasionally showing his face in this congenial and cosy maritime restaurant.

name: Da Vinci
review: In a prime city-centre location next to the theatre and opposite the Electoral Palace, the headquarters (dating from 1794) of the Deinhard family's wine trading company houses this modern restaurant. The decor is minimalist and elegant, the cuisine is classic and creative. The latter is the domain of Daniel Pape, who conjures up a set menu which is full of finesse. His career to date has taken him from one top chef to the next, from Dirk Luther to Thomas Bühner and from Christian Jürgens to Joachim Wissler. High-quality produce is the name of the game here, as can be seen, for instance, in the turbot served with asparagus and velouté sauce. Beyond the culinary delights, the service is also spot on – an attentive and accomplished front-of-house team; very good wine recommendations.

name: Wielandshöhe
review: Here in one of Stuttgart's most exclusive residential areas, set amid the lush vines, veteran chef Vincent Klink's Wielandshöhe stands proud. This restaurant is the epitome of elegance with its large windows that afford unobstructed views over the city. Chef-patron Vincent Klink and his right-hand man Jörg Neth deliver classic cuisine that draws inspiration from their Swabian homeland. They steer well clear of gimmickry and frills, instead employing their immense culinary skill to tease out the full flavours of premium ingredients. Unsurprisingly, this place has held a Michelin star almost continuously since 1993.

name: Adler
review: Having run this establishment with bags of charm and a sure touch for four generations, the Fehrenbacher family has made a real success of its restaurant – it has retained its Michelin star every year since 1990! Daniel Fehrenbacher, who took over the helm of this award-winning kitchen from his father Otto, is the man behind the outstanding modern French cuisine. He attaches great importance to showcasing what the region and the changing seasons have to offer, which is particularly evident in the game dishes. Interesting flavour contrasts are skilfully incorporated into the dishes. The winning combination of modern and classical elements also applies to the decor: a mix of chic, minimalist style and Black Forest charm. For connoisseurs of fine wines, the service team at the Adler offers astute wine recommendations.

name: Haus Stemberg
review: The culinary formula here is "two cuisines from one oven", with both modern and classic fare on offer. Running the show is Sascha Stemberg, who represents the fifth generation of the family behind this business started in 1864. He likes to combine regional traditions with modern, international trends, using quality produce all the while. The Big Green Egg grill is deployed to cook the tasty barbecue dishes. The Kuhlendahl pearl barley soup is a house specialty. A varied and well-chosen wine list includes some interesting rarities. The tradition that this inn suggests from the outside with its slate façade also makes itself felt inside: from the cosy restaurant room to the elegant lounge with fireplace and the winter garden, you will notice original details such as old wooden beams and panelling. Remarkably friendly service!

name: 1876 Daniel Dal-Ben
review: Classic and modern styles go hand in hand at Daniel Dal-Ben's restaurant. This Düsseldorf native of Italian heritage opened his small restaurant (located directly next to the zoo and ice hockey stadium) in November 2002. Since then he has demonstrated total dedication to his role as chef-patron. He builds on classical culinary foundations by adding just the right dose of creativity to great effect. Selected ingredients are combined to create harmoniously balanced, full-bodied dishes that are rich in finesse. Guests choose the number of courses they want to try from the set menu. Beyond the terrific food, the atmosphere is pleasingly relaxed and the wait staff are attentive and well trained.

name: Malathounis
review: Michelin-starred Greek cuisine? "Modern Greek cuisine" is what it says on the front door, and that's what you get at this charming, tastefully decorated restaurant run by a husband-and-wife team. The dishes are sophisticated and rich in flavour, interspersed with French influences and the light touch of Mediterranean cuisine. Chef Joannis Malathounis clearly draws inspiration from his Hellenic roots, yet he never relies on them too heavily. One essential ingredient is the high-quality olive oil! It's exciting to see this interpretation of Greek cuisine. There are two set menus, one of which is vegetarian, as well as a small à la carte selection. In the cosy dining rooms, guests are warmly received by the lady of the house, Anna Malathounis, in person. She is also happy to offer recommendations from the selection of fine Greek wines.

name: Zur Post
review: This restaurant has a certain something. From the outside, this historical inn flaunts its traditional character, while inside the elegant decor has a more modern touch. In the kitchen, brothers Alejandro and Christopher Wilbrand conjure up their ingredient-led and creative cuisine, showcasing their knack for interesting details and clever, highly original combinations of flavours and textures. The menu draws on regional culinary heritage as well as more far-flung European influences. Ask the wait staff for their judicious recommendations from the excellent wine list. In addition to the Michelin-starred restaurant and the less formal Postschänke, there is a small hotel with comfortable rooms, should you wish to stay the night. The Festsaal, complete with state-of-the-art kitchen, makes for a fabulous event venue.

name: Burg Nideggen - Brockel Schlimbach
review: What is it that makes this place stand out? First, the location in a 12C castle above Nideggen, boasting a fantastic view! Second, the attractive interior: a historical little dining room with modern design features and wood panelling throughout creates an atmosphere that is all of its own. Last but not least, there is the cuisine. An abundance of ideas, energy and passion makes itself felt in the modern set menu created by eponymous chef-patrons Herbert Brockel (previously of Erftstadt's Michelin-starred Husarenquartier) and Tobias Schlimbach (who also has plenty of experience in Michelin-starred gastronomy). It goes without saying that the fantastic dishes are prepared using the finest produce. While the chefs serve the food themselves, the ladies of the house recommend interesting wines.

name: La Bécasse
review: The location of this restaurant on the outskirts of the city centre may be rather inconspicuous, but by no means can the same be said of the food! Chef-patron Christof Lang has been welcoming diners in this well-maintained corner house since 1981. Together with chef de cuisine Andreas Schaffrath and their kitchen team, he serves up pared-back, no-fuss classic cuisine scattered with a few modern touches. The dishes are straightforward, but abounding with finesse, not to mention full flavours! Rest assured that only the finest produce is used. How about one of the wonderful French wines to go with your meal? These form the focal point of their appealing selection. The highly attentive service is charming and friendly; this place runs as smoothly as a well-oiled machine. A limited set menu is available at lunchtime.

name: Das Grace
review: A former naval building right on the marina houses sophisticated hotel The James, where you will also find the chic and elegant restaurant Das Grace. The 7m-high ceiling and chandeliers draped in silk make quite an impression, as do the views of the marina from some of the seats. The exclusive atmosphere is enhanced by the friendly and attentive front-of-house team, who serve up Quirin Brundobler's modern, seasonal cuisine. Much of the produce comes from the restaurant's own James Farm or from local fields, meadows and waters. Alternative dining options are to be found at James Farmhouse, with its open kitchens, and Japanese restaurant Minato. On top of that, you have The Lion bar as well as "Tea Time & More" by the fireplace in the James Livingroom.

name: PAVO im Burghotel Falkenstein
review: This restaurant proposes a "sharing experience" at an altitude of 1 250m – magnificent views included! Simon Schlachter wins over diners in this small restaurant with his modern cuisine. He has his own style, which is creative and elaborate. This is put to good use in the set menu, whose courses each consist of several small dishes that are perfect for sharing. The friendly and down-to-earth yet well-drilled front-of-house team takes good care of you and talks you through the individual courses. The interior is done out in royal blue with high-quality materials and features an artistic painting on the ceiling and decorative peacock feathers ("pavo" is the Thai word for "peacock"). Alternatively, try out Restaurant zu Pfronten with its regional cuisine. Tastefully decorated guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

name: Alt Wyk
review: If you would like to enjoy excellent food in a really feel-good setting, then make for this restaurant in a well-maintained brick building located in the pedestrian zone. The tasteful dining rooms are done out in an exceedingly cosy and elegant style that exudes plenty of Friesian charm. Chef René Dittrich is the man behind the sophisticated cuisine. He takes a classical approach to cooking and his dishes never fail to impress with their technical skill and beautiful flavours. Your hostess is Daniela Dittrich, who is in charge of the well-trained and attentive front-of-house team, who work together seamlessly to cater to diners' every need. Should you wish to savour this delightful spot near the sea a little longer, be sure to book one of the two really pretty holiday apartments.

name: Gasthof zum Bad
review: Taking over the family business was definitely the right decision! Chef Hans Häge has been at the helm of what used to be his parents' place since 2007, serving up classic seasonal cuisine with a modern twist that also draws on international influences. On the evening menu, for instance, you will find a Langenau venison saddle ragout with cauliflower, chanterelles and fregola sarda, or also red prawn and guinea fowl with fragrant cream of rice, mango and flavours of Asia. Although he insists on using only select ingredients, the prices are reasonable. The à la carte selection of dishes, including Maultaschen in broth and Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy), shows that the owner also knows his way around Swabian specialities. The modern yet cosy Gasthof zum Bad is also a popular choice for overnight stays.

name: Buchner Welchenberg 1658
review: The 16C estate has been in the family since 1882, and Mathias Achatz represents the fifth generation at the helm in the kitchen. Culinary talent is in his genes: his mother cooked to an extremely high standard before him! This chef-patron's dedication to his work makes itself felt in his cuisine, which could be summarised as a modern take on more classic dishes. Regional influences also feature on the menu, as well as one or two references to Asia. Beyond the delicious food, you can look forward to a pleasant atmosphere, which is largely down to the attentive and experienced front-of-house team. The chef's brother Andreas is responsible for putting together the first-class wine selection, although he is mostly busy with his own hotel, which is located 2km away.

name: L.A. Jordan
review: Hotel, restaurants, event venue – the former Bassermann-Jordan winery on the German Wine Route is all of the above. The chef de cuisine in the fine dining restaurant of this beautifully restored historical estate is Daniel Schimkowitsch. His style is modern, creative and pleasantly pared down. Steering clear of any gimmickry and relying instead on distinctly intense flavours, he whisks diners off on a culinary adventure. The desserts are sure to impress with their sophistication and originality. Interesting wine pairings complement the set menu. Then there is the service team, which is all that you could wish for: charming, accomplished and always on hand. Both the dining rooms here – one elegant, the other more on the trendy side – are chic and modern, and there is a wonderful terrace in the courtyard.

name: mural
review: What makes the food here so special? Youthful energy and real talent! This restaurant is housed in MUCA, the Museum of Urban and Contemporary Art, which is the inspiration behind the design of the eponymous mural. The dedicated kitchen team delivers an imaginative set menu that abounds with intense flavours. A vegetarian version is also available if you order in advance. Or perhaps you'd prefer fish? The produce is almost exclusively sourced from within Bavaria – the absolutely premium-quality trout, for example, is a real treat! Friendly and congenial service, with the chefs also occasionally getting in on the act. An appealingly straightforward take on wine – their selection includes some interesting natural wines.

name: Frieda
review: Friendly, refreshing, unpretentious – it's undeniably good fun to eat here. In addition to the pleasantly uncomplicated bistro atmosphere and chic design, the cuisine proposed by this pair of restaurateurs goes down particularly well. Lisa Angermann and Andreas Reinke offer ingredient-led modern dishes in the form of a monthly changing set menu dubbed "Frieda En Vogue" – alternatively you can opt for the vegetarian version, "Frieda Naturell". In keeping with the restaurant's ecological ethos, when it comes to choosing ingredients, the focus is on the region and the changing seasons. The friendly and accomplished front-of-house team is headed up by the charming proprietor. There is also a lovely terrace and orangery. Good to know: they also run a "gourmet farm" in Baldenhain – a mix of event venue, farm and manufactory.

name: Goldener Anker
review: The likeable TV chef Björn Freitag is a household name. In 1997, at the age of 23, he took over this long-established restaurant, breathing new life into the kitchen. In 2002 the place was awarded a MICHELIN star, which he and his team have held on to ever since. The setting is lovely, too: the decor is sophisticated and elegant, which is perfectly suited to the classically based cuisine with modern influences. The wonderful flavours of excellent produce are combined in an extremely harmonious way. The charming and accomplished front-of-house team will accompany you through the evening. There is also a cookery school in the same building.

name: Atelier Sanssouci
review: Atelier Sanssouci – the name alone sounds stylish, and this wonderful 18C estate certainly does not disappoint! Not only is the exterior of the Villa Sorgenfrei with its magnificent garden a veritable feast for the eyes, but the interior is also a sight to behold: the large dining room done out in an elegant Mediterranean style boasts remarkable chandeliers and a high stuccoed ceiling. The food is on a par with the setting. A successful blend of classic and modern cuisine, it draws on premium ingredients to produce subtle flavour contrasts and balancing acts. Wine lovers can look forward to exquisite wine pairings – the experienced sommelier is on hand with splendid suggestions.

name: Die Brasserie
review: Here, the informal atmosphere of a brasserie meets the sophistication of a Michelin-starred restaurant. Behind the striking red façade, a beautiful Mediterranean-style interior awaits. In the bistro area at the front of the premises, diners take their seats at high tables, while the restaurant area to the rear is furnished with comfortable wicker chairs set out beneath a decorative ceiling painting. For chef-patron Vjekoslav Pavic, the quality of the produce is paramount. His carefully considered dishes are perfectly balanced and intense in flavour – just what you wish for in a meal! The well-drilled front-of-house team is friendly and appealingly laid-back, which contributes to an ambience that puts guests at ease – this is especially true of your charming hostess. It's no surprise, then, that there are so many regulars. Head for the pretty terrace in fine weather.

name: Werners Restaurant
review: If you have always wanted to treat yourself to a spot of fine dining in the historical surroundings of a castle, then Schloss Eberstein is the place for you. Perched on a hilltop above the Murg Valley and surrounded by vines, it commands stunning views! Set on a magnificent historical estate, this lovely hotel with two dining options is run by the Werner family. The elegant fine dining restaurant has made a name for itself with its modern take on classical cuisine. Chef-patron Bernd Werner presides over a dedicated kitchen team that brings balance and intense flavours to the plate. The wine list also features a selection from the hotel's own vineyard – ask for recommendations.

name: Masa Japanese Cuisine
review: Word quickly spread that this inconspicuous townhouse in Frankfurt's Ostend district is home to a fantastic Japanese restaurant. Masaru Oae set up shop here in June 2021, just after having expanded his skills and his knowledge of the Japanese culinary arts in both of Yoshizumi Nagaya's Düsseldorf restaurants. In an unpretentious and pared-back Far Eastern-style decor, diners sit at the food counter or at small tables to enjoy expressive dishes that are full of finesse and flavour. The kitchen draws on both classic and modern Japanese cuisine, while remaining open to the odd European influence. It goes without saying that the young head chef is also a master in the art of making sushi and sashimi. Top tip: Experience the full range of his skills by ordering the omakase set menu, accompanied by sake upon request.

name: La Cuisine Rademacher
review: This place may not be located in the most attractive area (the city centre is not exactly around the corner), but it is very much worth visiting this pleasant restaurant done out in a chic and trendy bistro style. Inside what is an outwardly rather inconspicuous corner building, you will find a dedicated young team at work. After working at some top-flight establishments (including Waldhotel Sonnora in Dreis-Wittlich and Wein am Rhein in Cologne), and now in his own restaurant, head chef Marlon Rademacher shows that he has mastered his craft. He puts a carefully considered modern spin on dishes based on classical foundations. The ingredients always take pride of place. A vegetarian set menu is available – a vegan version is also possible if ordered when booking.

name: maximilian lorenz
review: Entirely dedicated to German cuisine, maximilian lorenz, located near the main train station, cathedral and the Rhine, offers a creative set menu that combines the modern and the traditional in a skilful and multifaceted way. Diners are sure to be impressed by the top-notch produce, the culinary skill of the kitchen team and the exquisite flavours. The interior is upmarket, elegant and minimalist. The extensive wine list has a very good selection of champagnes and sparkling wines. Wine lovers should also check out heinzhermann, the modern, laid-back wine bar located just next door, which boasts 1 200 wines from around the globe.

name: Marly
review: Speicher 7 is a monumental and spectacular landmark that stands out amid Mannheim's harbour landscape. It is home to Marly, an elegant and tastefully decorated restaurant run by Gregor Ruppenthal, a native of the Palatinate. Rooted firmly in French culinary tradition, his cuisine draws on ingredients from his own herb and vegetable garden, as well as from further afield, from the Mediterranean and Brittany, and these are complemented by plenty of organic and Demeter produce. You will be looked after by the friendly and competent service team who are anything but stuffy in their manner. In summer, make a beeline for the wonderful terrace facing the Rhine!

name: Le Jardin de France im Stahlbad
review: Sophie and Stéphan Bernhard have made it their mission to indulge the diners of this city since 1998. Since relocating, they welcome their guests here in the Stahlbad, a beautiful 19C building located in the heart of Baden-Baden. The classic French cuisine, which is in the blood of the chef-patron, a native Frenchman, is as much in great demand as it ever was. His clearly structured and wonderfully harmonious dishes give pride of place to high-quality produce. The front-of-house team, which includes the lady of the house, is exceptionally cordial and accomplished, and the wine recommendations are second to none – there is a very good selection to choose from.

name: Wullenwever
review: Roy Petermann has been at the helm of Wullenwever since 1990. His restaurant, which occupies a charming patrician house dating from 1585, proposes classic cuisine that is replete with Mediterranean influences and enjoyably free of gimmicks. The focus here is on top-quality produce, which is showcased in harmonious dishes. There is a set menu that changes every three weeks, as well as a surprise menu, which can be ordered in advance. Vegetarians are also catered for. The excellent wine list is principally devoted to labels from Germany and Europe, but it does also venture as far as the New World. The Hamburg-born chef runs this tasteful, elegant restaurant in the middle of the old town together with his charming wife, Manuela, who attentively looks after the guests. The inner courtyard with its lovely green terrace is wonderful!

name: Schwitzer's Sternerestaurant
review: Come to the fine dining restaurant of Schwitzer's Hotel am Park for a modern take on classic cuisine. Owner and head chef Cédric Schwitzer runs the show with total dedication. He relies on top-quality produce to ensure an abundance of flavours. These take the form of a set menu made up of a flexible number of courses. Alternatively, you can ask for the "Menu Surprise", which comprises a selection of the individual courses on offer – perhaps stay away from the menu altogether if you don't want to ruin the surprise! A nice touch: each dish comes with a little card bearing a photo and description. Exceedingly friendly service; savvy wine recommendations. The elegant interior with its floor-to-ceiling windows affords a beautiful view of the park.

name: KUNO 1408
review: This really lovely restaurant located in the centre of the Baroque city has a long tradition dating back over 600 years – to 1408, to be exact. At that time, Kuno von Rebstock is said to have been one of the first owners of the Zum Rebstock estate – hence the name. Today, diners can look forward to cuisine that trains its focus squarely on top-quality produce. The modern, creatively inspired dishes are brought to you by a well-drilled yet friendly and relaxed front-of-house team, who are able to give excellent advice on wine pairings. The restaurant itself is also pleasing on the eye, with its modern, elegant interior comprising chic armchairs, designer lamps and warm and earthy tones. For overnight stays, the Hotel Rebstock proposes comfortable, individualised guestrooms.

name: taku
review: A classic grand hotel like the Excelsior Ernst (dating from 1863) may not be the setting you would expect for a restaurant done out in a minimalist Asian style. But for all its classicism, the venerable establishment right next to the cathedral also has a chic, modern side, which taku fits into perfectly. The straightforward, elegant design is complemented by Mirko Gaul's contemporary and well-thought-out dishes. Successfully balancing spiciness, acidity and sweetness, he creates an aromatic fusion of East Asian cuisine and Western/international influences. Here and there, you will also find regional produce among the selected ingredients. Choose from the "Degustation" and "Veggie" set menus, from which you can also order à la carte. Very well-stocked wine list – with good recommendations by the glass.

name: Gourmet Restaurant im Schlosshotel Münchhausen
review: Dine like royalty in a castle setting! Could you ask for more splendid surroundings than those of the historical Schlosshotel Münchhausen, a stately home dating from 1570? After an aperitif in the imposing Rittersaal – a lobby with a fireplace – or in the Schwöbbar – next to the moat with views of the park –, guests take their seats at elegantly set tables in a refined restaurant done out with stucco ceilings, parquet flooring and paintings. Here you can enjoy classical French cuisine that also draws on Mediterranean and more modern influences. Then there is the friendly and competent front-of-house team.

name: Restaurant 1797
review: A picture-perfect setting! The centuries-old Gut Panker is set amid a charming landscape of forests and meadows. This magnificent property with an abundance of rural charm is known for being a Trakehner stud farm. As the business of the estate goes on around you, head chef Volker M. Fuhrwerk treats you to a creative and seasonal set menu. He focuses on select produce from the north of Germany – vegetables, fruit and herbs even come from his own garden. Sit back and enjoy the attentive and well-drilled service, as well as the recommended wine pairings by the glass. With its view over the green pastures and its shady old copper beech tree, the terrace is the perfect place to unwind. No less inviting is the elegant former hunting room with its extremely stylish rustic interior.

name: Le Gourmet
review: A truly delightful property with a long tradition of hospitality behind it: as early as 1472, guests were received in the Hirschgasse, across the river from the castle. Le Gourmet is the hotel's romantic, historical fine dining restaurant and it comes complete with old tiled stove, stylish parquet flooring and fabric-covered walls. Despite all the details retained from bygone days, this place is anything but stuffy, and this is largely thanks to chef Mario Sauer. He skilfully integrates modern elements into his classic cuisine to create dishes with complex flavours and plenty of finesse. The charming and highly efficient front-of-house team is led by sommelier Erik Himpel.

name: Oben
review: Idyllically set amid meadows and fruit trees overlooking Heidelberg, the historical hamlet of Kohlhof is something of a culinary island in the forest. The cobbled inner courtyard exudes a rural charm, making it the perfect spot for an aperitif. Head into the inviting dining area with its lovingly decorated interior and pleasingly intimate atmosphere. The open kitchen sends out a well-devised and modern 13-course set menu. Head chef Robert Rädel has a highly creative touch and brings regional and seasonal produce to the fore. Much of it is sourced in the local area, including the wine. The chefs also deliver the dishes and talk you through them. Only German wines are available – choose for yourself in the wine cellar! Be aware that this place books up fast – follow the link on Oben's homepage for last-minute spots. Rooms available in the Obendrüber studio.

name: Mühlenhelle
review: What a fabulous property! With this magnificent villa, Michael and Brigitta Quendler have opted for a highly distinguished setting in which to indulge their guests. Elegant style, warm tones, beautiful wooden floors, large mullioned windows – the overall effect is really inviting. Add to the location the attentive and competent service and Michael Quendler's cooking. Although predominantly a classic affair, his cuisine is still modern and enjoyably pared down – he is adept at weaving the different flavours of his excellent ingredients together on the plate. There are two set menus (one of which is vegetarian/vegan) featuring dishes you can also combine as you please or order à la carte. Excellent selection of wines by the bottle – you can rely on your charming hostess for recommendations! Comfortable guestrooms for an overnight stay.

name: Alte Schule - Klassenzimmer
review: Now this is a school you'll be happy to go to! And it is all down to Daniel Schmidthaler. In an idyllic setting, this native of Upper Austria serves up an exciting and modern surprise menu comprising seven courses in the "Klassenzimmer" where pupils once studied. The decor is simple and stylish, with charming features such as an old tiled stove, parquet flooring and tall mullioned windows. Alternatively, in the beautiful setting of the "Schulgarten" conservatory, you can sample a vegetarian menu made up of four courses. The cuisine echoes the chef's love of nature. Whether it's game, fish or mushrooms, he always works with fresh seasonal produce sourced from the immediate surroundings. He likes to employ aromatic herbs and the tartness of fruits in his dishes. Should you wish to stay the night, there are also bright and comfortable guestrooms.

name: The Stage
review: Michael Dyllong, who made his name in Dortmund's fine dining circles as the head chef at Palmgarden in Casino Hohensyburg, has had his new premises in the Hombruch district since September 2021. The seventh floor of the Dula Center makes for an appealing setting. Here, he and his team propose two very elaborately prepared set menus (one of which is vegetarian) that are both a real pleasure to eat. The service is extremely professional, thanks in no small part to restaurant manager and sommelier Ciro De Luca, long-time business partner of Michael Dyllong. The experience is rounded off by the chic, modern interior and magnificent views – on one side you have the Westfalenstadion, on the other a beautiful view of the surrounding area. Some seats allow diners to sneak a peek into the small open kitchen.

name: freustil
review: It is a real stroke of luck for the beautiful Baltic Sea resort of Binz that Ralf Haug, who was born in the Black Forest, has moved up to the far north of Germany. In 2013, he came to the Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten from Rügen's Michelin-starred niXe and has been wowing guests of the fine dining restaurant with his remarkable creativity and finesse ever since. Considering the first-rate quality of the ingredients, the value for money is surely worth a mention! On the menu, dishes such as mixed pickles with quinoa and malt or bavette steak with barbecue flavourings and coleslaw are indicative of the modern and imaginative cooking on offer here. The ambience is as pleasingly straightforward as the cuisine, which is largely down to the very friendly and attentive front-of-house team. Tip: Lunch is also available at a reasonable price.

name: Hannappel
review: Knut and Ulrike Hannappel's restaurant is a total departure from the pub that used to occupy this corner spot. Your hosts may have run this place since 1993 but they have never stopped evolving. The interior has been given a facelift and its tasteful, sleek design is now bang on trend. The exciting food is just as modern: innovative, technically sophisticated and pared-down dishes. Under the supervision of Knut Hannappel and head chef Tobias Weyers, the kitchen team brings its considerable technical skill to bear on top-notch produce. "Casual fine dining" sums it up perfectly. Rounding it all off is the attentive and professional front-of-house team, whose relaxed attitude adds to the pleasingly informal atmosphere. Note: From the beginning of January to the beginning of February 2023, you will find the "Hannappel" under the name "Pop-up in the LAURUShaus by Hannappel" at Schloss Hugenpoet in Augus-Thyssen-Straße 51.

name: tulus lotrek
review: Why is this restaurant run by Ilona Scholl and Maximilian Strohe so popular? For one thing, there is the gorgeous setting. Housed in a pretty old building in Kreuzberg, the dining area boasts high stuccoed ceilings, wooden floors, artwork and original wallpaper. For another, the informal yet well-drilled front-of-house team, which is headed up by Scholl, fosters a friendly, laid-back atmosphere. But it is of course primarily the cuisine that draws diners in. The chef-patron and his kitchen team use premium ingredients to devise really interesting combinations. Their secret? Vibrant stocks and sauces that bring the different flavours together beautifully and give the dishes that certain something. It will make you want to order another course!

name: Bembergs Häuschen
review: Come to the beautiful centuries-old castle complex of the von Bemberg family to experience fine dining amid stately surroundings. The adjoining 18C manor house is home to an exceptionally attractive, modern and elegant restaurant, whose minimalist yet stylish interior complements the character of the historical farm building. Chef-patron Oliver Röder and chef de cuisine Filip Czmok use exquisite produce to conjure up well-balanced, aromatic and inventive dishes. Diners are made to feel completely at home here, which is largely down to the extremely attentive, charming and competent front-of-house team. For those who wish to savour the tasteful setting a little longer, there are five individually decorated and really comfortable rooms available in the "Nachtquartier", which was once the cowshed!

name: Cheval Blanc
review: Katharina and Christian Fleischmann are the seventh generation to run this family business. They have close ties to the region and its producers. Meat and sausages come from their own butchery; game, lamb and pigeons from producers they know well. Their classic cuisine is full of interesting flavours and displays a modern touch. Available as part of a set menu or à la carte, the cleverly pared-down dishes are very well thought out, and each is served in three variations. Soak up the atmosphere of this traditional gourmet restaurant in the small dining room done out in an elegant style. The warm and friendly lady of the house is also part of the charming and attentive front-of-house. Overnight guests can make the most of tastefully decorated rooms and a beautiful spa area.

name: SIEDEPUNKT
review: Who would expect such a restaurant in a business hotel? In the annexe of the Atrium Hotel you can look forward to a stylish interior done out in chic grey tones – the striking wall of glass wine refrigerators is bound to catch your eye. Seated at elegantly set tables, diners are looked after by a friendly and professional front-of-house team. Thanks to its elevated location, the terrace with its beautiful view is also in demand! This sophisticated setting is complemented by modern, seasonal dishes prepared using high-quality produce. The "KunstHandwerk" set menu is also available in a vegetarian version. Nice to know: non-hotel guests can park free of charge.

name: Sterneck
review: A breathtaking view of the North Sea, the Elbe world shipping route and the UNESCO-listed Wadden Sea – quite a backdrop for the first-class cuisine on offer at Badhotel Sternhagen. This is the domain of Marc Rennhack, who has worked at several of Juan Amador's restaurants, including, most recently, Heritage by Juan Amador in Bucharest. His modern cooking builds on classical culinary foundations. With consummate skill, he lends dishes a sense of creative flair and conjures up interesting flavour combinations. His set menu comes in three to seven courses. Take a seat at your elegantly set table to enjoy the dishes and the friendly service.

name: Gasthaus Jakob
review: Although you'll definitely need to look up the way to this little 250-year-old country inn, it's well worth making the effort: really comfortable surroundings (in summer there is also the terrace at the front of the house) and charming service await you. The fine cuisine on offer is not what you would necessarily expect so far off the beaten track in the middle of the Bavarian Forest! Head chef and owner Michael Klaus Ammon adheres to classic culinary tradition, but also incorporates modern ideas, resulting in expressive dishes such as roasted lobster soup served with baked lobster or a pleasingly light yoghurt crème brûlée. Incidentally, the team supporting this native Upper Franconian includes his partner Mona Haka and his brother Andreas, who oversee the front-of-house team together. Appealing wine pairings by the glass.

name: BODENDORF'S
review: The fine dining restaurant of the gorgeous Landhaus Stricker proposes a fun culinary experience that comes courtesy of the team led by Holger Bodendorf and Denis Brühl. Meticulous work goes into preparing a six- to nine-course set menu comprising clearly structured dishes based on classical foundations. Top-notch ingredients are used to create aromatic flavour combinations with elaborate little details. The setting is also impressive: bare oak tables and modern artworks lend the place a touch of freshness – an ideal backdrop for the competent young service team, who look after the guests in their friendly and pleasingly casual manner. Astute wine recommendations are also provided – they have over 900 labels. Tip: Head to the trendy Miles Bar for an aperitif before dinner.

name: Kin Dee
review: This urban, informal and youthful spot more than lives up to its name (in Thai kin dee means "eat well"). A unique experience awaits you in this outwardly rather unassuming building that lies off the beaten tourist track. Here, Thai-born Dalad Kambhu proposes exceptionally authentic Thai cuisine. She combines selected produce from Brandenburg with winning contrasts of typical Asian flavours to create dishes that are intense and pleasantly spicy, but not too hot. You will be treated to a set menu that comprises a few little appetisers to begin with, followed by a main course of your own choice and a small dessert. The wine list also features a selection of natural and orange wines. A word to the wise: be sure to peruse the short cocktail menu.

name: Balthasar
review: It is not for nothing that Elmar and Laura Simon have long proved popular with diners: Balthasar has held a Michelin star continuously since 1999! Chef-patron Elmar Simon originally set up shop here in 1996. His right-hand woman is his charming wife Laura, a sommelier by profession, who, together with her front-of-house team, takes a pleasingly relaxed yet professional approach to her guests. On the way into the elegant restaurant, the porthole in the entrance area affords a sneak peek into the heart of the operation – the kitchen –, increasing your anticipation of their modern take on classic cuisine all the more. Vegetarians are catered for with the "Grüner Garten" ("Green Garden") set menu.

name: Maître im Landhaus Kuckuck
review: Erhard Schäfer is one of the grand masters of classic culinary art in the cathedral city. He has been at the helm of this small fine dining restaurant located in an appealing setting close to the stadium since 2009. Prior to that, he served Michelin-starred cuisine in Cologne's Börsenrestaurant Maître. His "tournedos Rossini à la Escoffier" – an instant classic – is a good example of his brand of cooking: old-school but with modern influences. That the chef holds himself to high standards is plain to see in his choice of first-rate produce as well as his excellent sauces and stocks. The attentive and professional service is as classical as the cuisine and the setting. Alternatively, there is the second restaurant, Landhaus Kuckuck, with its fabulous terrace beneath the old trees and large sunshades.

name: REISERS am Stein
review: With its incredible location above the city and amid the vines, this place is a real gem! Take a seat in the trendy, lively wine bar – with its superb view over Würzburg – or in the more elegant restaurant. Chef Bernhard Reiser and his team serve up classic cuisine with a modern twist, and they don't hold back when it comes to creativity. The flavour combinations may be somewhat unconventional, but they are always harmoniously balanced. Opt for the "Freistil" ("Freestyle") menu and select your own ingredients from a given list. Fine dining is available from Thurs to Sat; on the first three days of the week, the apprentice chefs show off their skills with a range of reasonably priced three-course set menus. Incidentally, the owner is a connoisseur of Franconian wine – so he also proposes wines from the neighbouring Weingut am Stein.

name: Délice
review: Too bad there is only room for a few guests in this beautiful vaulted restaurant! But that is just as much a part of the restaurant's special charm as the extremely courteous, warm and competent service, which is a matter of pride for Evangelos Pattas – this Belgian of Greek descent and a remarkable host puts his heart and soul into everything he does. This applies to the wine recommendations, too, because he also is a sommelier who appears to have almost encyclopaedic knowledge of his subject! The open kitchen is single-handedly run by Andreas Hettinger. Using very good produce, he prepares a seasonal set menu that clearly draws on classical, Mediterranean and creative influences. If you wish, you can reduce the five courses of the menu to four.

name: Landhaus Feckl
review: Manuela and Franz Feckl are truly exemplary hosts. They have been running their establishment since 1985 and their dedication is plain to see – not least in the kitchen. The dishes display a sure touch and stand out for their premium ingredients and first-rate technical skill. Choose from "Franz Feckl's classics" or from various set menus, including a low-carb and a vegetarian version. The reasonably priced lunchtime menu is also popular. Be sure to try the handmade spaetzle! Wine lovers will appreciate the good selection here, which features one or two rarities. The elegant country-house style makes for an appealing atmosphere on the restaurant floor, which has cosy seating niches – from the window seats you can look out over the fields. The friendly lady of the house also oversees the front-of-house team. There are pretty guestrooms for overnight stays.

name: Christian's Restaurant - Gasthof Grainer
review: The Grainer family has been running this stately historical inn since the 16C, and today it is Christian F. Grainer and his wife Christiane who form a real dream team at the helm! He is responsible for the exquisite and classically French cuisine, which also allows itself excursions into more modern trends; she is your dedicated hostess and sommelier. Their appealing surprise menu is stripped down to the essentials, better to maintain its focus on the premium ingredients. The intimate atmosphere in this cosy and elegant restaurant is largely down to the welcoming lady of the house, who is on hand to provide charming and accomplished service. She also has plenty of excellent wine recommendations at the ready – there are more than 1 000 different labels (including rarities and large bottles) stored in the old vaulted wine cellar.

name: GOLVET
review: Stepping out of the lift on the eighth floor of the Loeser & Wolff building, you will immediately be impressed by the sensational view over Potsdamer Platz and the city! But that is by no means all: this spacious restaurant set up in the rooms of the former 40 Seconds Club is strikingly stylish with its open kitchen and 13m-long bar – they may well have the largest aquavit selection in Germany! And then there is the service and the food – both of the highest calibre. Chef Jonas Zörner's team conjures up modern, creative cuisine with a focus on quality produce and original ideas. There is also an impressive wine list featuring small organic producers. Alternatively, you could opt for the house-made kombucha to go with your meal.

name: La Société
review: Everything is just right in this small fine dining restaurant in the student quarter of Kwartier Latäng, from the service to the ambience to the cuisine. Not only has it been given a tasteful, modern facelift, but the chef is also a new addition. Since August 2021, Leon Hofmockel has been bringing his own fresh ideas to the table. With consummate skill, he conjures up subtle contrasts, plays with acidity and textures and creates a beautiful balance. The result is intelligently structured dishes full of surprising flavours. Meanwhile, the service is second to none: in a friendly, lively atmosphere, your dedicated host Stefan Helfrich and his team have a cordial and courteous approach to each guest – everyone clearly enjoys what they are doing, which simply cannot fail to put you in a good mood!

name: Alfredo
review: If you are looking for authentic Italian cuisine in Cologne, Roberto Carturan is your man. His father, Alfredo, laid the foundations for upscale Italian cuisine in 1973, and the second generation of the Carturan family has cultivated a straightforward and minimalist style of cooking. The chef himself is responsible for the friendly, informal and elegant atmosphere: he likes to spend time with his guests and talk them through the dishes. Besides cooking, Roberto Carturan has another talent: he is a trained singer – on Friday evenings there's the "musical culinary soirée": a five-course menu with a bout of singing as the finale! One practical tip: Parking is available in the Opern Passagen shopping centre located behind the restaurant. You might also take the opportunity to see the original 4711 store with its famous carillon.

name: Schwarzer Adler
review: This establishment is steeped in tradition. Since summer 2018, Christian Baur has been at the helm of the kitchen in the legendary Schwarzer Adler – owner Fritz Keller (whose mother Irma was awarded a Michelin star back in 1969) is fully supportive of Christian Baur's bid to continue cooking in the classic French style that has become synonymous with this place. This cosy, stylish and elegant restaurant will be of particular interest to wine lovers. The cellar includes some wines from the house winery, which has been in the family for three generations. Tasteful guestrooms are available should you wish to stay the night. You also have the option of dining at Winzerhaus Rebstock, which serves up simpler and more traditional fare.

name: Genuss-Apotheke
review: All that remains of the pharmacy that once stood here is the tribute contained in this establishment's name. These days, a restaurant with a bold, modern design awaits you behind its large windows. Seated at beautifully laid tables in a bright, minimalist interior, diners' eyes are naturally drawn to the open kitchen. Here, chef-patron Raimar Pilz puts together creative and pleasingly pared-down dishes – the produce is top-notch, from the tender Eifel-raised lamb to the aromatic crab. Fragrant herbs are an integral part of the seasonal dishes. A fine dining set menu of five to eight courses is served every evening. The friendly and attentive service comprises astute wine recommendations.

name: Gutshaus Stolpe
review: On this beautiful estate, a cobbled driveway leads to the carefully restored historical manor that is home to this elegant restaurant. Reminiscent of an English country house, it fits into the charming and stylish setting perfectly. The chef at the helm is Christian Somann, who worked here in previous life. Since mid-2022, after stints at some renowned establishments, he has been back, serving up technically sophisticated dishes full of bold flavours and finesse. High-quality produce goes into his set menu. Wonderful terrace overlooking the grounds, tastefully decorated rooms for an overnight stay.

name: Elements
review: With its industrial-style architecture, loft feel and elegant, upmarket interior, Elements is a chic restaurant run by Martina and Stephan Mießner in the historical Zeitenströmung building complex. He heads up the kitchens; she is in charge of the friendly and smooth front-of-house service. The spacious and high-ceilinged interior boasts floor-to-ceiling arched windows, beautiful floorboards and comfortable brown leather chairs with a vintage look. The dishes are pleasantly well defined and pared down with plenty of expression and finesse – order à la carte or opt for the "chef's menu". Lovely terrace on Times Square. The casual DELI offers a more casual alternative from noon.

name: NeoBiota
review: Breakfast or fine dining? Here you will find both under one roof. Proprietors Sonja Baumann and Erik Scheffler are a duo of chefs who ran the kitchen at Gut Lärchenhof in Pulheim together. They have now struck out on their own at this restaurant in the centre of Cologne, where they have been serving up a two-pronged dining concept since May 2018. Expect a modern restaurant with zero pretensions, plus an open kitchen and an appealingly straightforward atmosphere. A delicious breakfast complete with great home-baked bread is served at Neo from 10am until 2.30pm. In the evening, at Biota, there is an excellent seasonal set menu composed of four, six or eight courses – it is available in either its conventional format or a vegetarian or completely vegan version. Evening service runs from 7 to 11pm.

name: SoulFood
review: Here, Christine Heß and Michael Laus really deliver on their extremely appealing "soul food" concept. After working side by side at Frankfurt's Villa Merton, the two have fulfilled their dream of owning their own restaurant with this establishment located right next to Auerbach's town hall. And what is it that makes this place such a hit? On the one hand, it comes down to their warm and friendly welcome, which sets the tone, and on the other, it is their fabulous, creative cuisine made from top-notch seasonal produce, which is also reasonably priced. Diners are given a choice of two set menus: "DasEine" or "DasAndere". The dishes draw on inspiration from Asia as well as the Mediterranean, without losing sight of the local region. A beautiful, modern restaurant that makes for a simply delightful dining experience!

name: Alte Pfarrey
review: This pretty centuries-old vicarage blends into its picturesque surroundings perfectly. Michelin-starred chef Silvio Lange and his wife Bettina moved back here in 2015 – he actually ran the Alte Pfarrey's kitchen once before many years ago. Your friendly hosts serve up creative, seasonal cuisine that is prepared using top-notch produce. There are two set menus to choose from. Would you prefer to dine in the beautiful historical restaurant or in the bright and modern conservatory, which is elegantly done out with solid wooden tables and affords a view of the original building? In both dining areas, you can expect friendly and well-drilled service and expert wine recommendations. Outside, the splendid inner courtyard beckons. Tasteful, individually decorated guestrooms are available should you wish to spend the night.

name: Ente
review: This is the epitome of classic fine dining! The luxurious Nassauer Hof grand hotel dating from 1813 provides the stylish setting for the elegant Ente. Diners sit at exquisitely set tables laid out over two levels – a curved staircase with wrought-iron bannisters leads up to the gallery – and have their every need catered to by an attentive and well-drilled front-of-house team. The high-end interior and service are more than matched by Michael Kammermeier's cuisine. A mostly classic affair, it also features the odd modern touch, in the agreeably subtle form of interesting contrasts of flavour and texture. Choose from two set menus: "Die Ente" and "Küchenrunde". You might like to head to the terrace laid out to the front of the building.

name: Landhaus Scherrer
review: Heinz O. Wehmann is to Landhaus Scherrer (which has a spruce new exterior!) what St Michael's Church is to Hamburg! Since 1980 he has been head chef in this restaurant that was opened by Armin and Emmi Scherrer in 1976 (and awarded one, and at times even two MICHELIN stars as of 1978). For years the outstanding regional, often organically certified produce has been par for the course here. As classic as the interior – the large-format erotic painting remains the decorative focus! – are also the dishes. The Holstein venison, served with an excellent rosemary sauce, for instance, is absolutely fantastic. The wine cellar, which has grown to over 10 000 bottles, is also impressive! The service is attentive and professional, but by no means stuffy. For an alternative to gourmet cuisine, head to Wehmann's Bistro for good regional dishes.

name: La Vallée Verte
review: Picturesquely situated in a gorgeous landscape of forest and meadows, this wonderful stately home and castle (dating from 1901) was originally laid out as a manor. In the small restaurant, chef-patron Peter Niemann and his head chef Denis Jahn present a set menu of up to ten courses featuring dishes that are well balanced and brimming with finesse and intensity. They use excellent produce that they hunt and farm themselves, and successfully incorporate the flavours of Brittany and Scandinavia into their fish and seafood dishes. The highly attentive and competent front-of-house team will also be able to help when it comes to expert wine recommendations. Overnight accommodation available at Hotel Schloss Hohenhaus.

name: Ratsstuben
review: Not only does the small Ratshotel in the middle of the old town have attractive, comfortable guestrooms, it also boasts an appealing restaurant. Chef-patron Daniel Georgiev prepares a modern set menu using select produce and drawing on international influences. Great wine selection comprising over 250 labels. Friendly and attentive service. Elegantly minimalist interior done out in bright, warm tones. If you prefer quality home-style cooking, Gute Stube serves steaks and the like. Outside there are a few tables laid out in the pedestrian zone.

name: ernst
review: Somewhat unprepossessing from the outside, inside this is a stylish and creative space. There are just eight seats at the long wooden counter, and these are in great demand – facing the large open kitchen, diners sitting here come into contact with the team of chefs as they compose a set menu made up of a whole series of delicious little dishes. The wonderful smell from the charcoal grill is also worth mentioning! Proprietors and head chefs Dylan Watson-Brawn and Spencer Christenson impress with a clear, refined and often subtle style that draws heavily on Japanese cuisine. This is food that makes the produce sing, so you can expect the unadulterated flavour of premium ingredients to come through. The wine pairings are also fun. Bear in mind that booking is via an online ticket-purchasing system. There are two sittings per night.

name: Maerz - Das Restaurant
review: Modern tastes meet regional flair! Brothers Benjamin and Christian Maerz propose a successful blend of both in the fine dining restaurant of their Hotel Rose, hitting the mark in two different respects. First, the interior with its gorgeous wood panelling and clear lines makes for a chic and fashionable yet cosy ambience. The cuisine, too, draws on regional culinary tradition as well as contemporary trends, in the form of a set menu dubbed "Heimweh/Fernweh". The chef uses first-rate ingredients (preferably sourced in the local area) to turn out well-structured dishes that are pleasingly pared-down and brimming with clever marriages of flavours. Christian Maerz will be happy to talk you through the wines or non-alcoholic options. There is a pleasant lounge terrace on which to enjoy a pre- or after-dinner drink.

name: Silberdistel
review: The Sonnenalp Resort, which has been run by the Fäßler family since 1919, is definitely worth a visit for anyone interested in fine dining. Silberdistel's kitchen team uses select seasonal ingredients, which they make a point of sourcing from the region. Diners choose between classic dishes ordered à la carte and the "Weitblick" set menu. Here on the fourth floor, you are afforded wonderful views, so be sure to ask for a window seat. Having said that, the restaurant interior itself, with its blend of stylish elegance and Alpine charm, is also a sight to behold. Then there is the enthusiastic sense of hospitality, which makes itself felt throughout this traditional establishment.

name: ESS ATELIER STRAUSS
review: Upscale furniture fashioned out of recovered wood, comfortable designer chairs upholstered in lovely check fabrics, edelweiss-shaped lighting fixtures set into the ceiling, and pared-down, elegant tableware – this restaurant has a fresh and modern decor. But it isn't just the chic Alpine look that guests go in for. The dishes conjured up by chef Peter A. Strauss are equally inspiring. You will be treated to pleasingly stripped-down classic cuisine that takes inspiration in modern, creative trends. The ingredients are always first-rate. Check out the 18m2 glass-walled and temperature-controlled wine cabinet! Diners can choose from around 300 different wines from Germany, France, Austria and Italy.

name: Cookies Cream
review: Finding your way here through a maze of backyards to ring the bell at the unassuming door is an adventure in itself! An old stairway leads you up to the first floor, where you'll find this vibrant restaurant done out in an "industrial" style. This trendy spot was once a fashionable nightclub, but today it serves 100% vegetarian Michelin-starred cuisine to a soundtrack of electronic music. Head chef Stephan Hentschel is at the helm in the kitchen. His dishes are well thought out, clearly structured and meticulously prepared – they take the form of a set menu consisting of five to seven courses. The service is cool and casual, but no less professional and well organised for it. A youthful and appealing concept that hits the mark – the mixed clientele from hipsters to bankers to families speaks for itself!

name: Sankt Benedikt
review: Aachen's Sankt Benedikt has been an established part of North Rhine-Westphalia's Michelin-starred fine dining scene since 1982. In the wake of the recent disastrous floods, the Kreus family was only able to reopen its restaurant at the beginning of December 2021 after a tremendous effort. This was much to the delight of diners, who can once again enjoy Maximilian Kreus's classic cuisine in this listed building in the historical centre of Kornelimünster. His dishes always centre on the finest produce, which he sets about with plenty of feeling and a dash of originality. The service is extremely friendly, and expert advice regarding the wines is readily available – only wines from German wine producers are recommended.

name: Laurentius
review: The Koch family business has virtually all of your needs covered, with its lovely accommodation on the Marktplatz, terrific food and ever-obliging service. Owner Jürgen Koch and his wife Sabine have made it their mission to champion regional cuisine in their modern and elegant dining room with its distinctive natural stone barrel vaulting. Prepared using top-notch seasonal produce, dishes eschew frills and fancy flourishes in favour of finesse, harmony and plenty of flavour. There are fine wines from the Tauber Valley, Franconia or Baden-Württemberg to complement your meal. The wine list also features a selection from France, among other countries. Insider tip: head to the Hohenloher Märktle to stock up on some nice ingredients to take home with you.

name: BECKER'S
review: In keeping with the architecturally interesting design hotel of the same name, a high-quality fine dining restaurant done out in a chic, minimalist style awaits you here. The interior boasts leather shell chairs, elegant parquet flooring and grey panelling on the walls – a lovely setting in which to enjoy a very ingredient-led set menu to the sound of modern background music. Proprietor and head chef Wolfgang Becker deliberately steers clear of gimmickry and instead focuses on flavour. Not only is your host a cook but he also has a penchant for fine wines. He trained as a winemaker and wines from his own vineyard also feature on the wine list.

name: Maltes hidden kitchen
review: In the middle of the pretty pedestrian zone of this well-maintained spa town, you will come across this interesting dual concept of coffee shop and restaurant. Coffee and cake are served here during the day, while in the evening the kitchen team, headed up by eponymous proprietor Malte Kuhn, proposes modern dishes – prepared in the "hidden kitchen" tucked away behind a sliding panel.
