They skilfully pare things down to the essentials, making the ingredients the focus of the set menu. The service is extremely friendly and professional, with the cooks also getting in on the act and the owner always on hand, too. A pleasant, cosy little restaurant with a charm all of its own – dining here makes for a really fun experience!

name: Pottkind
review: Enrico Sablotny and Lukas Winkelmann, the duo who run this little restaurant, are from the Ruhr Valley. The cuisine here is exciting: modern, flavoursome, it is made with top-notch ingredients. It may be predominantly plant-based but that doesn't mean you have to miss out on fish and meat altogether. Diners never know what to expect from the carte blanche set menu. Excellent service comes courtesy of very attentive, competent and charming waitstaff, who give the place a pleasantly unpretentious feel. The seats at the counter overlooking the open kitchen are especially popular. In summer, soak up the lively atmosphere of Cologne's Südstadt district on the terrace.

name: Weinstock
review: Diners can expect a wonderfully chic ambience on the first floor of the traditional Zur Schwane hotel, where the modern decor blends harmoniously with the beautiful historical building. Having taken your seat at leather-covered tables, relax and enjoy the attentive service. In the kitchen, Cornelia Fischer and her dedicated team demonstrate their talent for delivering dishes that home in on the essentials: the selected ingredients and the flavours always take pride of place. Opt for the suggested wine pairings, which accompany the excellent food beautifully. Here, they serve fine wines from the region, some of which come from the adjoining winery – happily, all of the "Schwane" wines can be ordered by the glass. Attractive, individually decorated guestrooms are available, should you wish to stay the night.

name: Gut Lärchenhof
review: When Peter Hesseler started out here in 1997, he could never have dreamed that this place would one day make a name for itself as a Michelin-starred restaurant. Since 2017, Torben Schuster has been at the helm in the kitchen of this gorgeous estate on the high-ranking golf course. His cooking is modern, bold and creative, but never loses sight of its classical foundations. This successful fusion of styles gives rise to unusual dishes – many of his concoctions have what it takes to become signature dishes! Host Peter Hesseler and his friendly and well-trained team provide excellent service, including sound wine advice. We recommend heading out to the lovely terrace, which is sure to give you that holiday feeling!

name: Mod by Sven Nöthel
review: What a beautiful spot! Sven Nöthel has opened his elegant restaurant in a lovingly renovated stable surrounded by lots of greenery. The sleek modern design is just as eye-catching as the open kitchen, which gives you the feeling of being part of the action. This chef's talent is clear for all to see in his beautifully balanced dishes, which demonstrate just the right dose of creativity (served on earthenware crockery made in Wesel). He works with exceptional ingredients and has a preference for regionally sourced produce. There are also plenty of vegetarian ingredients to be found on the menu, which follows the seasons. The service is warm and friendly – even the chefs get in on the act and talk you through the dishes. Pretty terrace, too.

name: Schote
review: The likeable restaurateur and TV chef Nelson Müller proposes a winning dual concept in Essen's city centre. The modern building complex at Rüttenscheider Stern houses not only the bistro MÜLLERS auf der RÜ, but also his fine dining restaurant Schote. In the large open kitchen, a set menu of four to ten courses is created, with excellent produce that is meticulously transformed into expressive dishes. The vegetarian "No Meat No Fish" is also available by prior arrangement. Staff are happy to recommend the right wine to go with whatever you opt for. The interior is modern yet cosy, and the service is very friendly, attentive and competent.

name: Hämmerle's Restaurant - Barrique
review: A charming, long-standing family business that sticks to what it does best with the classic cuisine of Cliff Hämmerle. Working with top-notch produce is a matter of course for him – and this also applies to the vegetarian menu. The wine pairings are superb. This is the domain of hostess and sommelier Stéphanie Hämmerle, who together with her daughter Emely cordially and attentively manages the front-of-house team. The bright and modern interior is tastefully and elegantly done out, complete with glass-paned wine cabinet. Tip: The second restaurant, Landgenuss, also welcomes diners at lunchtime. A modern and comfortable suite makes provision for overnight stays.

name: Restaurant Villa Merton
review: André Großfeld has already proven his skills in his restaurant Grossfeld in Friedberg, and continues to consolidate his reputation in the elegant Villa Merton. Together with head chef Philippe Giar, the chef-patron brings together classic and modern culinary styles to produce creative, sophisticated dishes that are harmonious and full of flavour. It goes without saying that the quality of the produce is second to none. This listed villa in the diplomatic quarter also provides a prestigious setting for your fine dining experience: high ceiling with stucco work, gorgeous parquet flooring, stylish wallpaper, fireplace… In addition, the terrace to the rear of the restaurant is a really pretty spot in which to enjoy your meal. Then there is the friendly, professional front-of-house team, always on hand yet pleasingly unobtrusive, who serve you at elegantly set tables.

name: SKYKITCHEN
review: It is worth making your way out to Lichtenberg: up here on the 12th floor of the Vienna House Andel's Berlin you have a fantastic view over the city. An urban-chic atmosphere prevails, all the better to enjoy Alexander Koppe's impressive cuisine. The native Berliner (most recently sous-chef at the Lorenz Adlon Esszimmer) brings together Mediterranean, Asian and regional influences in two modern set menus dubbed "Voyage Culinaire" and "Vegetarian". Check out the wine list with a twist: beyond the German and Austrian labels, it only features Slovenian, Slovakian, Polish and Bulgarian wines. Once you've soaked up the stylish vintage ambience here, you may want to head up a couple more floors to Loft14 for a digestif.

name: Schiller's Manufaktur
review: You can be sure of a high culinary standard at Hotel Stein, thanks to chef-patron Mike Schiller and his Mediterranean-inspired classic dishes. These are proposed in the form of an appealing à la carte menu, alongside a range of "Meisterwerken" ("masterpieces"), such as bouillabaisse, and daily specials, such as tri-tip cut of Wagyu beef. While the vegetarian "Garden Menu" is always available, the "Classic Menu" and seasonal "Special" need to be ordered in advance. Out on the restaurant floor, the friendly maître d', Melanie Stein-Schiller, is in charge of service. You can sit in the inviting dining room, the bright conservatory or out on the charming terrace in the garden. Top tip: head to the shop for home-made delicacies to take away.

name: Lamm Rosswag
review: Even in a sleepy little wine village like this, you don't have to do without creative Michelin-starred cuisine! Here, the modern and intelligently devised dishes are full of harmony, interesting details and the best ingredients. And the chef clearly has a knack for producing intensely flavoured sauces. Thanks to your warm and friendly hosts, the atmosphere in the Ruggabers' long-standing family business doesn't disappoint either. The service is pleasingly informal yet professional; the wine recommendations are spot on – there's a decent German selection to choose from. The set menu on Wed and Thu evenings is a slightly reduced version compared to at the weekend. The lunchtime menu is also somewhat less elaborate. If you order in advance, you can get a vegetarian version of the set menu. Good accommodation is also available.

name: Schlossberg
review: Schlossberg has been a culinary institution in the idyllic Murg Valley for decades. Now it has been given a stylish makeover: modern shapes, pale wood and serene hues of grey and beige, complemented by discreet art on the walls. A well-rehearsed father-and-son team, Jörg and Nico Sackmann offer internationally influenced dishes, mostly put together with a dash of modern flair, sometimes pared down, sometimes complex. It goes without saying that only the finest produce is used. The individual courses of the two set menus – one of which is vegetarian – can also be combined. The front-of-house team is highly accomplished, helpful and attentive. For overnight stays the beautiful guestrooms and elegant spa area of the Hotel Sackmann are just the ticket.

name: Wein- und Tafelhaus
review: In this little winemaking village, Daniela and Alexander Oos have turned a former winegrower's house dating from 1672 into a lovely fine dining restaurant where guests really feel at home. While the chef-patron cooks up Mediterranean-inspired, seasonal, classic cuisine, the proprietress takes charge front of house, winning over diners with her easy Tyrolean charm. The savvily devised and pleasingly unfussy dishes made from premium ingredients are accompanied by a great wine list that is principally devoted to regional labels. Diners take their seats in a glass-walled cube that has an elegant modern interior and commands marvellous views of the famous Trittenheimer Apotheke vineyard on the other side of the Moselle. Outside is a pretty garden right next to a small vineyard. A number of tasteful guestrooms are also up for grabs.

name: Yoshi by Nagaya
review: Yoshizumi Nagaya's Michelin-starred cuisine can now be sampled in two different locations in Düsseldorf. Not far from the original restaurant, also located in "Japantown", Yoshi opened in October 2016. The food here is classic Japanese, untouched by Western influences. In the evening, the omakase set menu wins over diners with its absolutely ingredient-led and exceedingly precise preparation. It is accompanied by a large selection of sakes. In a way, the interior is a reflection of the pared-down style of the dishes: the restaurant has a minimalist design. Come along at lunchtime to enjoy a cheaper set menu. Lots of the diners are Japanese – which speaks for itself!

name: Der Zauberlehrling
review: Wine lovers will be delighted to see the walk-in glass wine cabinet upon entering the restaurant – it gives a first impression of the 300 or so labels on offer here. The chic interior with its stylish, minimalist design and distinctive details is also sure to draw the eye. This makes for a pleasant atmosphere, as does the charming and accomplished service. A sophisticated setting such as this serves as a perfect backdrop for head chef Fabian Heldmann's contemporary cuisine: rich in contrasts yet beautifully balanced, it bowls diners over with its depth of flavour. Be aware that on Saturdays they only offer their "Candle Light Dinner". For overnight stays, the small design hotel of the same name boasts a central location and tasteful, individually decorated guestrooms.

name: Falconera
review: In a verdant setting close to Lake Constance, this converted mill is an appealing spot with a fabulous garden. It is a centuries-old half-timbered house, in which the Falkenstube and Mühlenstube dining rooms are done up in a tasteful blend of elegant and rustic decor. The many regulars keep coming back for more not only on account of the gorgeous space, but also for the friendly welcome extended by the hosts. On top of that, there is the outstanding cuisine, which demonstrates passion and skill. Chef-patron Johannes Wuhrer draws on fresh, selected produce to cook up classic seasonal dishes. Opt for the "Falconera" set menu or the vegetarian "Gemüsemenü" – alternatively you can order dishes à la carte. At lunchtime there is also a cheaper three-course set menu.

name: Kunz Gourmet
review:
Temporarily closed.
Representing the second generation to run this family business, Anke and Alexander Kunz form a well-established team. While the enthusiastic hostess presides over the restaurant floor, the chef-patron, together with head chef Patrick Jenal, turns out pared-down dishes that steer clear of unnecessary frills. The focus lies squarely on flavour and excellent produce. The glass front of the elegant modern conservatory affords a splendid view of the impressive St Remigius Church, which dominates the Blies valley. In addition to the set menu served in the fine dining restaurant, you can also order from the "Kunz Traditionelle" menu – feel free to ask! Alexander Kunz is also known for his event catering and the dinner show "Alexander Kunz Theatre" in Saarbrücken.

name: Erno's Bistro
review: For many years, this has been a permanent culinary fixture in Frankfurt – and a really charming one at that, because here you feel like you're in a bistro in France. The charming, neighbourly atmosphere is partly down to the decor (pretty wooden panelling, decorative accessories such as wine bottles, pictures and lamps), and partly to the friendly, relaxed yet adept front-of-house team led by owner Eric Huber. Under the tutelage of head chef Valéry Mathis, the cooking is refined and rich in flavours. Expect French cuisine with seasonal and modern influences, and made using top-quality produce. In the extremely well-stocked wine list, also French, you will find the ideal accompaniment – the recommendations are spot on. This formula goes down very well with an international business clientele, as well as regulars from the local area.

name: Das Maximilians
review: Das Maximilians is the flagship of the Fetz family's restaurants. In the small fine dining restaurant of the family-run Das Freiberg Hotel, head chef Henrik Weiser and his enthusiastic kitchen team use top-quality ingredients to deliver well-devised modern dishes that demonstrate great technical skill. The plush, elegant interior is instrumental in creating the pleasant atmosphere, as is the attentive and competent service, which is largely down to the friendly lady of the house, Margret Bolkart-Fetz. When it comes to wine, you can rely on the staff to give suitable recommendations.

name: Schloss Loersfeld
review: The centuries-old castle with its extensive grounds really is a magnificent property. Behind the massive stone walls, stylish guestrooms and lounges with antique details await. This stately backdrop makes for a fabulous setting in which to relish the modern cuisine with classic foundations. Not only are the dishes a feast for the eyes, they also stand out for the quality of their ingredients, their expressive flavours and technical finesse. Be sure to check out the Graf Berghe von Trips exhibition in the Grüner Salon. Should you wish to stay over, an adjacent building houses overnight guests in three pretty apartments.

name: Rüssel's Landhaus
review: The charm of this country house makes itself felt as you approach via a small bridge – it is safe to say the character of the idyllic old mill has been successfully preserved! Ruth and Harald Rüssel clearly put their heart and soul into running their hotel and restaurant. The chef-patron and his talented kitchen team propose a five- to seven-course set menu. Diners are won over by the quality of the ingredients, which they prefer to source from local producers; they even hunt their own game. The classical foundations of the cuisine always shine through, but are elegantly complemented by creative flourishes that never come across as fussy or unnecessary. Try out the surprising wine pairings – they tend to recommend fine Moselle wines. Head to the terrace to sit by a small lake! They also have appealing guestrooms.

name: Leos by Stephan Brandl
review: Rustic wood features and original decorative touches combine to create a high-end, minimalist decor here. Beautifully situated in the Bayerwaldhof spa hotel, which overlooks the village, Leos is a modern take on a small "Stube" (or parlour), with no more than five tables available. The chic look and pleasantly informal atmosphere are complemented by a relaxed yet highly efficient service team and well-thought-out, clearly structured dishes that come courtesy of chef Stephan Brandl, who hails from the Upper Palatinate. A set menu of five or eight courses, all of which are made from premium ingredients, showcases his culinary skill. The range of wines that can be ordered by the glass is also well-judged. Nice to know: if you dine here as a hotel guest, you pay a much lower price for the set menu!

name: Nobelhart & Schmutzig
review: This restaurant on Friedrichstraße may look unassuming but it pursues a philosophy all of its own. Proprietor and sommelier Billy Wagner (who previously worked at Berlin's Rutz) and head chef Micha Schäfer (formerly of Villa Merton in Frankfurt) prize the ingredients and the way they are sourced above all else. It goes without saying, then, that they use only the finest seasonal and regional produce in their cooking. They even make their own butter. This is well-thought-out and pared-down cuisine, which allows each component to tell its own story. The chefs themselves talk you through the dishes, whether at your table or at the counter next to the open kitchen – these seats are in particularly high demand! There is a ten-course set menu, accompanied by extremely interesting wines, beers and spirits.

name: Le Flair
review: Dany Cerf is the chef-patron behind this restaurant, which has a minimalist design and an elegant touch. Hailing from French-speaking Switzerland, he cooked up a storm under Jean-Claude Bourgueil and at renowned establishments such as the Baur au Lac in Zurich before opening Le Flair together with his partner Nicole Bänder in 2014. Here, he bowls diners over with his pleasingly straightforward, well-thought-out dishes, made from excellent produce and proposed in the form of a four- to six-course set menu. His penchant for classic French cuisine is evident, but he remains open to more modern influences. Head straight for the fabulous terrace in summer.

name: Bandol sur mer
review: So you wouldn't expect Michelin-starred cuisine in this casual and low-key restaurant done out in a "shabby-chic"style? Admittedly, the small dining area is a little rough around the edges: the furnishings are rather sombre and unostentatious, the bare tables are positioned close together, and the dishes are written on large blackboards all over the walls. In the open kitchen, Andreas Saul (formerly sous-chef at the Rutz Weinbar) demonstrates remarkable passion, precision and originality. His cuisine draws inspiration from the region and incorporates forgotten herbs and vegetables. Have you ever tried wild garlic kimchi or nettle puree? These are extremely well-devised dishes, harmonious down to the last detail and full of unique flavours. High-end dining paired with a pleasingly down-to-earth atmosphere.

name: prism
review: This restaurant located in the Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf district draws diners in with a chic, minimalist decor and exciting cuisine. In his Levantine-inspired creations, owner Gal Ben Moshe gives a nod to his Israeli roots as well as to modern European standards. Made from excellent ingredients, his interesting dishes are replete with contrasts in flavour. Beyond the fantastic gastronomic diversity on display, what really impresses here is the sense of a highly personal touch that you won't find anywhere else. To complete the picture, first-rate wines as recommended by Jacqueline Lorenz, a much-lauded sommelier and the extremely friendly lady of the house. Among the 230 labels on the wine list, there are fine wines from Israel, Syria and Lebanon to be found. All wines are also available by the glass.

name: Ostseelounge
review: There's so much to rave about here that it's hard to know where to start. The wonderful seaside location behind the dunes complete with fantastic views? The charming and professional service? The elegant yet relaxed atmosphere? However, the jewel in the crown of this fine dining restaurant on the fourth floor of the luxurious Strandhotel Fischland has to be the dishes conjured up by André Beiersdorff and Matthias Stolze. Theirs is a modern take on classic cuisine that draws on regional and occasionally international influences. The wine pairings for the set menu are excellent – or opt for one of their appealing house-made non-alcoholic alternatives. Don't miss the opportunity to enjoy an aperitif on the fabulous terrace!

name: Seven Swans
review: The location is out of the ordinary, as is the philosophy behind the cuisine! This restaurant is housed in the city's narrowest building, which is nevertheless seven storeys high. The stylish and sleek interior boasts fantastic views of the River Main through large floor-to-ceiling windows. On the menu: 100% vegan cuisine made from organic produce. Permaculture is the name of the game here, meaning only those regional ingredients that have been produced ecologically and in harmony with nature are used in the dishes. In keeping with this ideology, many of them come from the restaurant's own local farm. Head chef Ricky Saward has a knack for interesting and creative flavour combinations that may seem rather unusual at first glance but actually come together beautifully. Diners are waited on by the chefs themselves.

name: Jungborn
review: This elegant restaurant with its wonderful vaulted sandstone ceiling and atmospheric feel more than on a par with the rest of the imposing hotel complex. The excellent cuisine comes courtesy of Philipp Helzle, who has worked at Aqua in Wolfsburg and Ketschauer Hof in Deidesheim, to name but two. His cooking style is modern and creative; dishes such as the rabbit served with cauliflower, hazelnut and pear are technically very sophisticated, not to mention made with excellent quality produce. A cordial front-of-house team will be happy to recommend wines from the region to pair with whichever of the two set menus you opt for. Incidentally, the name Jungborn is a direct reference to this place’s original incarnation as Felke-Jungborn Kurhaus Dhonau and is a nod to the healthy-living ethos behind this hotel concept.

name: Piment
review: What makes this restaurant so charming? In addition to the beautiful interior decor with its warm tones and the friendly, competent service, Wahabi Nouri's cuisine should be mentioned first and foremost. You can really feel his total dedication and passion for cooking! The starting point is always the ingredients: his two set menus are based on the finest seasonal produce, which he skilfully uses to create harmoniously balanced creations using spices, and drawing out flavours and acidity. He works with considerable technical skill, sometimes diving deep into the details, and conjures up numerous nuances in his dishes. His cooking owes its personal touch to his respect for his heritage: Nouri comes from Casablanca, so he incorporates subtle North African influences that make his Moroccan vegetable tart, for example, a real taste sensation.

name: Schattbuch
review: Firmly established in the Allgäu fine dining scene is the trendy and elegant Schattbuch. Here, former sous-chef Sebastian Cihlars and Nico Lanz (son of well-known chef Anton Lanz) are the team behind the scenes. When putting together their modern dishes, they always look to the region for inspiration and give pride of place to high-quality produce. Creative finesse and a down-to-earth attitude go hand in hand. Thus a reinterpretation of the classic "Grandma's soup pot" goes down just as well as the saddle of venison or freshly caught sea bass. While in the same building, practically next door, robots are being manufactured, the ambience here is pleasingly natural and friendly – Christian Marz's front-of-house team is laid-back yet highly accomplished. Head for the terrace in summer.

name: Ich weiß ein Haus am See
review: In an idyllic spot in the middle of nowhere, somewhere between Berlin and Rostock... you will find this small hotel on a lonely lake. But it's not just a cosy place to spend the night: food-wise you'll also get your money's worth. In this elegant restaurant with its country-house flair, your hosts Petra and Adi König charmingly and courteously ensure that the feel-good factor is present. Meanwhile, Raik Zeigner devotes himself to cooking up classic cuisine, which has always had a solid reputation in this establishment. For his four-course set menu, which is different every evening, the best of ingredients are used. Take, for example, the "Müritzwald" venison saddle, served with garden vegetables, chanterelles, parsley puree and juniper sauce. Owner Adi König – virtually a walking wine encyclopaedia – unfailingly recommends the perfect pairings.

name: Gourmet-Restaurant Der Butt
review: The quality of this fine dining restaurant more than lives up to what the impressive Yachthafenresidenz Hohe Düne offers its hotel guests in terms of comfort and spa facilities. The modern cuisine with agreeably well-defined flavours comes courtesy of André Münch, who brings his culinary know-how and precise craftsmanship to bear on pared-down, intense dishes that abound with beautifully balanced flavours. This is how you showcase first-rate produce to great effect. A prime example of this is his wild Atlantic turbot, served with solena sweet yellow tomatoes and elderflower. In addition to the culinary delights, there is a visual highlight in store: the location on the top floor of a pavilion-style building affords a fantastic view of the marina – particularly stunning at sunset.

name: THE IZAKAYA
review: This trendy, casual eatery could be described as a "Japanese-Palatine pub". Benjamin Peifer (known for Intense in Kallstadt) and Yannick Schilli propose a fabulous fusion of local and Japanese cuisine in their take on an omakase set menu. High-quality regional ingredients are transformed into beautifully balanced dishes that are full of interesting contrasts. They put their Josper oven to good use, introducing smoky grilled flavours into dishes such as soy-glazed spare ribs with sweet onion cream, Koshihikari rice and warm bean salad. Be sure to ask the front-of-house team for their recommendations when it comes to the excellent wines, which you can also buy to take away in the adjoining wine shop, Rohstoff. For your information: the "Otoshi" will appear on your bill; this is a typical Japanese izakaya bar cover charge, which includes water and a snack.

With a name like 360°, who isn't expecting a great view? The highlight of this sleek, modern restaurant on the third floor has got to be the roof terrace! But you can also enjoy the views over the city from the inside thanks to the large windows. Alternatively, you can watch Alexander Hohlwein and his team at work in the open kitchen as they prepare their creative "Weltreise" set menu. Heading up the front-of-house team is his partner, Rebekka Weickert, your cordial hostess who also offers expert advice on wine – a non-alcoholic alternative is also available. The set menu is also available for lunch on Fri and Sat. From Wed to Sat there is an additional, pared-down lunch menu. Incidentally, they have a bee colony on the terrace and produce their own honey. Our tip: Park in the underground car park of the WERKStadt shopping centre.

name: Hupperts
review: Hupperts is somewhat hidden away in the middle of a residential area in the south of Stuttgart. Don't be fooled by the rather underwhelming exterior of the building, because behind the door you will find a tasteful interior and a charming, very attentive and experienced front-of-house team. But most importantly, chef and owner Michael Huppert also serves up a sophisticated set menu that is best described as "modernised classic". He puts the focus on the excellent, predominantly regional produce and, without any fuss, ensures finesse and expressiveness, including cleverly integrated contrasts of flavours.

name: Aubergine
review: The gourmet restaurant of the luxurious Vier Jahreszeiten Starnberg is the place to experience fine dining in a business hotel setting. Aubergine is situated in a glass-walled extension reminiscent of a conservatory. The upscale, modern decor finds its culinary counterpart here in the bold, creative cuisine of Maximilian Moser. International influences and the changing seasons both make their mark on his set menus. Top-quality produce, meticulous craftsmanship and intense flavours are complemented by beautiful presentation. The staff are courteous and competent, and the wine advice is also second to none.

name: Lakeside
review: Step out of the lift on the seventh floor of The Fontenay hotel and you will find yourself in the unique restaurant of this imposing hotel. In this airy and light-filled space, diners are bowled over by its bold design in elegant white, as well as its frankly sensational views over the city and the Outer Alster. The modern cuisine conjured up by Julian Stowasser is available as a set menu comprising four to six courses. Complex but never cluttered dishes, premium ingredients, meticulous craftsmanship. Michel Buder heads up a beautifully trained front-of-house team: relaxed yet professional, efficient and experienced – plus excellent wine suggestions from sommelier Stefanie Hehn. Treat yourself to an aperitif before dinner in the smart bar on the sixth floor and then take the curved staircase up to the restaurant.

name: Schwabenstube
review: Dedicated, cordial and consistent service is the name of the game in the Ottenbacher family establishment, a fact which can be put down to their long tradition of hospitality, spanning four generations to be precise! Here, they cultivate tradition and yet continue to evolve – as you can see in the spruce half-timbered house with its green shutters, where historical charm meets more modern and elegant design features. Max Speyer (who was formerly sous-chef here) produces classic cuisine that also draws on the region for inspiration. His expressive and coherent dishes incorporate what the season has to offer. Those who enjoy a fine wine with their meal can look forward to a very well-put-together wine list and equally sound recommendations. Comfortable guestrooms.

name: PHOENIX
review: Close to the Schauspielhaus and the Hofgarten with its theatre museum, Düsseldorf's well-known and architecturally striking Dreischeibenhaus houses an appealing restaurant. The interior boasts a stylish mix of 1960s design and modern features, as well as an open kitchen. Here, Philipp Wolter presides over the creation of classic dishes that seek inspiration in modern culinary tradition and international cuisine. The quality of the produce is on a par with the finesse, balance and technical skill on display. In the evening, choose from set menus known as "Flora" and "Fauna" plus à la carte dishes. At lunchtime they offer an à la carte selection as well as their "Quicklunch". The front-of-house team led by restaurant manager Tanja Wolter is friendly and experienced. On the first floor, the Bel Étage is available for private functions.

name: Im Schiffchen
review: If we're talking about Michelin-starred cuisine in a beautiful Baroque brick building on Kaiserswerther Markt, we can only be talking about Jean-Claude Bourgueil's Im Schiffchen. At the helm since 1977, he is without a doubt the doyen of Düsseldorf's fine dining scene. Together with his tried-and-trusted kitchen team, Bourgueil delivers creative French cuisine. Whether it be lobster, game or Wagyu beef, the produce is of the finest quality. To complete the picture, there's the impressive selection of wines, the attentive and well-trained wait staff and the gorgeous decor – this ground-floor restaurant has a tasteful maritime look.

name: DR.KOSCH
review: The concept is a hit: a beautiful modern gastro-bar with a friendly, informal atmosphere, paired with unconventional cuisine at reasonable prices. This is all down to Volker Drkosch. The award-winning chef from Lauf an der Pegnitz in central Franconia has already seen plenty of action on Germany's fine dining scene: he has served as head chef in Michelin-starred restaurants such as Portalis in Berlin, Brick Fine Dining in the Main Plaza hotel in Frankfurt and Victorian in Düsseldorf. He uses outstanding produce to create exciting dishes that abound in interesting flavour combinations. One real signature dish is the umami bolognese, made with Rotes Höhenvieh beef, mature parmesan, wasabi salad and horse mushrooms. Tip: The bar affords a direct view into the kitchen.

name: Bieberbau
review: For those who appreciate not only really good food but also a fantastic setting, this is the place to be! Dating back to 1894, this listed building has been wonderfully restored – Richard Bieber's stucco craftsmanship in the dining area is truly worth seeing! In this unique location, diners are looked after by a friendly and competent service team led by hostess and sommelier Anne Garkisch, while chef-patron Stephan Garkisch cooks up modern dishes at the Molteni stove. He skilfully showcases herbs and spices in his set menus (one is vegetarian), with much of the produce coming from his own garden. Good value for money.

name: Erbprinz
review: The Erbprinz has long been a culinary institution in the area. And quite rightly so as anyone who has sampled Ralph Knebel’s classic cuisine, continuing its tradition of excellent food, will confirm. The dining room is lovely with a light and elegant interior, although in summer there is nowhere more delightful than the outdoor terrace.

name: Eckert
review: This fine dining restaurant is as chic as the designer hotel of the same name. Whether in the conservatory or the lounge area, the modern, minimalist decor feels both cosy and stylish. In the kitchen, young chef-patron Nicolai Peter Wiedmer demonstrates his mastery of classic cookery as well as his creative flair – he also likes to incorporate Asian flavours. In the evening, the set menu ("Lieblings Momente") can also be served in a vegan version. At lunchtime, two smaller tasting menus (one vegan) are served, as well as the business lunch. The fabulous wine list comprises around 450 labels, with recommendations to pair with the set menu. In summer, head out to the lovely terrace.

name: Storchen
review: Classic fine dining cuisine or more regional fare? With its set menus dubbed "Der große Storch" and "Einfach Storchen", the Helfesrieder family ensures that every guest is catered for. This place is run with dedication by two different generations. When choosing their ingredients, Jochen Helfesrieder and his father Fritz attach great importance to seasonality – the vegetables, herbs, flowers and fruit are grown in their own farm garden. The focus is on select produce from the surrounding area, although international influences can also be found on the menu. This picture-perfect traditional Baden inn dating from 1764 has tastefully decorated dining rooms – opt for rustic charm with an old tiled stove and wooden panelling, or a more modern setting. There is also a pretty garden terrace with a pond. Cosy and comfortable guestrooms.

name: Friedrich
review: In this immaculate townhouse on the diminutive Hans-Callmeyer-Platz, Lars Keiling wins over diners with modern French cuisine into which he incorporates creative twists as well as various flavours from the Mediterranean and beyond. Choose wines by the glass to pair with the four to seven courses on the menu, or solicit the expert advice at hand. Highly attentive to every guest's needs, restaurant manager and sommelier Gina Duesmann is in charge of the charming and professional front-of-house team. The fabulous food and pleasant service are complemented by the tasteful, chic and elegant interior. Alternatively, try the Kleiner Friedrich bistro, which boasts a beautiful terrace under shady chestnut trees.

name: Reuter
review: Founded in 1894, this family business has a long tradition – you're in good hands. In the beautifully refined and elegant restaurant of the hotel of the same name, Iris Bettinger has made a name for herself with her set menu, which boasts regional, Mediterranean and international influences. After working at the Hotel Colombi in Freiburg and Käfer-Schänke and Mandarin Oriental in Munich, she moved here in 2007 – making her the fourth generation at the helm. She creatively combines regional and seasonal produce, sourced from farms in the area as far as possible. The service is friendly and professional; the enthusiastic sommelier will talk you through the 250 wines on the well-curated list. Tip: On Wed and Thu the "TWENÜ" offer is available for guests under the age of 30 upon reservation.

name: Waidwerk
review: This is the culinary flagship of the Rottner country hotel. The small fine dining restaurant of this traditional family-run business now has the youngest generation at the helm, in the form of Valentin Rottner. He and his team propose a creative menu with bags of personality. Sommelier Thomas Wachter heads up the front-of-house team, overseeing the friendly and professional service with plenty of wit and charm. The interior is equally sophisticated, with the minimalist style made even more refined by a decor replete with rustic touches and hunting theme – this is no coincidence, for the head chef is a keen hunter. Valentin Rottner has already worked in some impressive kitchens, with stints at the two-star Söl'ring Hof on Sylt and the Gourmetrestaurant Lerbach in Bergisch Gladbach.

name: Dobler's
review: This place is something of an institution in the "City of Squares", so be sure to book well in advance. For more than 30 years, Gabriele and Norbert Dobler have been delighting their guests with outstanding cuisine that is rooted in tradition but by no means outdated. There is no need for showmanship when you have top-notch ingredients and technical skill as impressive as this. The bright, simple and elegant dining area is the domain of your charming hostess, who manages the front-of-house team. She is certainly one of the reasons why so many regulars have kept coming back for so many years. The extensive set menu is available at lunchtime too – as is a smaller lunch menu and à la carte dishes. Wine lovers will enjoy the appealing selection of labels from the region.

name: Alte Überfahrt
review: This place boasts a delightful setting on the waterside promenade of a small island in the Havel and the restaurant itself is equally attractive with its upscale, modern and elegant interior and almost intimate atmosphere. Then there is the creative cuisine, which is predominantly vegetarian. The dishes are characterised by their precise technical skill, clear structure and beautiful sense of balance – it is plain to see that head chef Thomas Hübner has already plied his trade in some of Germany and Italy's top restaurants. Owner Patrick Schwatke – himself a Michelin-starred chef – runs the show front of house, adding a personal touch to proceedings.

name: kochZIMMER in der Gaststätte zur Ratswaage
review: The 18C Ratswaage is exceedingly stylish! On the outside you have the historical façade, on the inside a minimalist interior with chic details such as silver-grey walls, 50s-style chandeliers and orange-red designer chairs. Here, the Frankenhäuser family and their team promise a culinary style dubbed "new Prussian cuisine". Head chef David Schubert presides in the kitchen, working with only the very best produce, preferably sourced from Brandenburg producers. Choose between two set menus, one of which is vegetarian, and be sure to consult owner Jörg Frankenhäuser when it comes to selecting your wine. Tip for the summer: try to get a table in the gorgeous courtyard – but be aware that places are limited!

name: sein
review: Located in a quiet residential street, this small restaurant spills out onto the pavement in summer. The tasteful, modern interior incorporates smart, high-end furnishings, setting the tone for Thorsten Bender's creative cuisine. This comes in the form of two set menus: "querbeet" ("at random") and "grünzeug" ("green stuff" – the vegetarian alternative), both available in six or seven courses. The chef-patron uses selected ingredients to conjure up well-thought-out dishes featuring interesting combinations, with Asian-inspired flavours a constant source of felicitous culinary contrasts. Then there is the friendly and accomplished service – Thorsten Bender and his kitchen team also like to get in on the act. At lunchtime they propose a three- or four-course set menu.

name: Veles
review: Head to Nuremberg's trendy Gostenhof district for a fine dining experience in a rather alternative setting. Chef-patron Vadim Karasev places the emphasis on regionality and seasonality in his restaurant. Many of the ingredients come from small producers in Knoblauchsland ("garlic country"), which is just down the road. In addition to the excellent quality of the ingredients, you can expect plenty of finesse and depth of flavour in the five to seven courses making up the well-thought-out set menu. Trendy decor, a relaxed and down-to-earth atmosphere, as well as a friendly and enthusiastic front-of-house team to take care of you and regale you with culinary delights.

name: JUWEL
review: This fine dining restaurant run by the Schumann family is aptly named, starting with a plush interior done out in chic lilac and black tones and including carefully chosen details such as amethysts and Swarovski crystals. Then there is the modern and creative cuisine, which also draws on more classic culinary traditions. This is the domain of Robert Hauptvogel, head chef here at Juwel since summer 2020. The exquisite patisserie courtesy of Beatrice Tobias also deserves a mention. One last feel-good factor rounds off the experience: the extremely friendly and accomplished service team led by Patrick Grunewald, who will also be able to advise you on wine. Top tip: They have a highly respectable champagne selection!

name: Les Deux
review: You will find Katrin and Fabrice Kieffer's smart restaurant on the first floor of a modern building in the heart of the old town. Diners take their seats in a triangular room with floor-to-ceiling windows that afford a view of the hustle and bustle of the city below. Nathalie Leblond is at the helm in the kitchen, sending out modern French dishes that can be ordered as a set menu or à la carte. The preparation is meticulous, the combinations innovative, the interplay of textures and temperatures skilful. Headed up by owner Fabrice Kieffer – your dedicated host and sommelier – the front-of-house team is extremely friendly and enthusiastic, as well as adept at providing expert recommendations when it comes to a wine list of over 500 labels.

name: Gourmetrestaurant Dichter
review: If you don't take the side entrance, you can reach this fine dining restaurant via the lobby of the luxurious Parkhotel Egerner Höfe, just beyond the elegant bar and decorative glass wine cabinets. The setting is upmarket, slick and modern, with three Japanese holly trees housed in striking glass cubes immediately drawing the eye. Floor-to-ceiling windows afford views out onto the grounds dotted with sculptures. The set menu ranges from five to nine courses, plus "Kellermann's classic dish". As well as showcasing regional cuisine, the food draws on traditional French fare and various international influences. Attentive and friendly service; excellent wine recommendations from the sommelier. Treat yourself to the wine pairings.

name: Oswald's Gourmetstube
review: The culinary heart of the Hotel Oswald! Head downstairs to the fine dining Gourmetstube, a spacious, refined, almost luxurious restaurant, the likes of which you would hardly expect to find here in Kaikenried (population 550) in the Bavarian Forest! Head chef Thomas Gerber presides here, having previously worked for many years as sous-chef at Heinz Winkler in Aschau and before that at Christian Bau in Perl. His finely balanced set menu draws on first-class produce and modern culinary trends. Choose a bottle from the nicely curated wine list (around 350 labels) and enjoy the attentive, ultra-friendly service. Upon request: "Dinner-Highlight" in the wine cellar (six to eight people).

name: Tantris DNA
review: Collectively called "Tantris Maison Culinaire", you will now find DNA just next to Tantris. This is a celebration of classic French cuisine à la carte and pays tribute to the renowned chefs previously at the helm: Eckart Witzigmann, Heinz Winkler and Hans Haas. The classics of the grand masters from five decades of this Munich institution are skilfully reproduced by a kitchen team that puts its own, slightly different spin on them, but the menu also includes new creations by the extremely talented French chef Virginie Protat. You will be well looked after by the charming maître d' and sommelier Mathieu Mermelstein – he will suggest exquisite wines from one of the most interesting wine lists in the country to accompany dishes such as the scallop served with Jerusalem artichoke and black truffle. The Burgundy is superb!

name: Gotthardt's
review: This restaurant in the Fährhaus Hotel is very stylish indeed with its sleek interior done out in soothing warm brown tones, and floor-to-ceiling windows commanding views over the Moselle. Diners can look forward to a pleasantly laid-back atmosphere, as well as friendly, attentive and professional service. And then there is Frank Seyfried's cuisine. The former head chef at Andernach's Ristorante Ai Pero serves up a modern take on classic and Mediterranean-influenced dishes, which you can order à la carte or compile to compose your own set menu. Vegetarians are also well catered for. Alternatively, the hotel has a second restaurant called Landgang, which boasts a beautiful terrace.

name: Steins Traube
review: Thanks to the commitment of the Stein family, what began in the early 20C as a village tavern has evolved over the decades into a modern restaurant serving sophisticated cuisine. Owner and head chef Philipp Stein represents the sixth generation at the helm. His outstanding culinary talent is such that there is no need for ostentation or gimmicks in his dishes. What may, at first glance, seem simple is actually exceedingly complex in terms of flavour and harmony, yet accessible for all that. His dishes demonstrate a restrained elegance, but he is also able to draw on a bolder sense of innovation when he deems it necessary. Choosing where to sit is not easy, because the smart and modern yet cosy interior is just as inviting as the beautiful inner courtyard. Friendly service comes courtesy of Alina Stein, your cordial young hostess.

name: [KOOK] 36
review: This welcoming, modern restaurant located in a quiet residential area is run by a highly dedicated team. In the kitchen, chef Daniel Klein never loses sight of the changing seasons and likes to source his produce from the surrounding area. Not only are his dishes beautifully presented, they are also full of flavour – thanks to the carefully selected ingredients! You can choose an "upgrade" in the form of judicious wine pairings. The chef's friendly partner, who manages the front-of-house team, is also on hand to make helpful suggestions. If you fancy an aperitif or digestif, you can take a seat in the lounge in comfortable Chesterfield armchairs. The terrace is also delightful.

name: Johanns
review: If you are looking to combine real fine dining with designer shopping, then why not head to the second floor of the renowned Garhammer shopping complex? Take a seat in the sleek, sophisticated surroundings to enjoy Michael Simon Reis's innovative cuisine. The Passau-born chef-patron has an aptitude for combining creativity with culinary tradition, all the while placing great value on produce sourced from the region. The unbeatable value for money is also worth mentioning. Head to the terrace for fantastic views of the region.

name: Ahlmanns
review:
Temporarily closed
Housed in an elegant former banker's mansion dating back to 1911, this stylish place has retained its historical feel, successfully combining it with modern minimalist design and warm tones. This is Ahlmanns, the fine dining restaurant of the tasteful Hotel Kieler Kaufmann. The high standard of the cuisine is down to Arne Linke, who wins over diners with meticulously crafted dishes made using the finest produce. Also worth a mention is the enthusiastic front-of-house team led by Björn Urbach. And don't be surprised if the chefs themselves approach your table to talk you through the dishes. Tip: On warm summer evenings, make a beeline for the really gorgeous terrace overlooking the park. As a more casual alternative, Kaufmannsladen also offers steaks and burgers.

name: faelt
review: Set in a listed building dating from 1903, this restaurant is run in a down-to-earth yet professional and carefully considered way – and that goes for the atmosphere, the service and the food. Incidentally, the name of this place is the Swedish word for "field" – a nod to the Nordic roots of head chef Björn Swanson and the ingredient-led style of cooking cultivated here. He and his team are inspired by the changing seasons, and plant-based ingredients take centre stage in the modern set menu. You can watch the chefs at work as the kitchen is practically part of the dining area in this friendly, vibrant little establishment – perfect for a cosy get-together.

name: Genuss-Atelier
review: 14 steps lead you down to this friendly, cosy cellar restaurant, where sandstone walls and brick vaults make for a special atmosphere. In a beautiful old villa in Neustadt, siblings Marcus and Nicole Blonkowski prove just how well an informal atmosphere and award-winning cuisine can go hand in hand – you can also enjoy your meal on the charming terrace. Marcus Blonkowski (who has worked with, among others, Silvio Nickol in the fine dining restaurant of the Palais Coburg in Vienna and Christian Bau in the Schloss Berg in Perl-Nennig) wins over diners with his interesting, modern and creative cuisine prepared using top-quality produce – and the value for money is hard to beat! The wine list features exclusively East German wine producers, and they have made a point of including some lesser-known ones. Conveniently located close to a bus and tram stop.

name: Yunico
review: The name of this restaurant fuses the Japanese word "yu" and the Italian word "unico", hinting at the food served here. "Yunico" is also a reference to the uniquely high culinary standards they uphold. Situated on the top floor of the Kameha Grand lifestyle hotel, thanks to its floor-to-ceiling windows the restaurant affords a fantastic view of the Rhine – a view which is of course even better from the terrace. Then there is the smart, high-quality decor, all done out in red, black and white, as well as the experienced and well-coordinated front-of-house team. Head chef Christian Sturm-Willms delivers a highly contemporary take on Japanese cuisine that also looks to the Mediterranean for inspiration. Opt for the omakase menu if you want to be surprised. Alternatively, choose from the Ōsentikku set menu or the "Filet & Roastbeef" (Kobe beef).

name: Grammons Restaurant
review: A culinary experience that inspires joy! In the middle of a well-tended residential area, in a pretty house with a pointed gable, is this delightfully bright and modern restaurant run by Dirk Grammon. The open kitchen sends out a tasting menu, which can be supplemented with an extra dish dubbed "Das kleine Extra". "Signature Fingerfood" to start with: "Zweierlei von Parmesan und Olive". This is classic cuisine, full of finesse and full-bodied flavours. Be sure to peruse the extensive and reasonably priced wine list. There is also a wine bar with terrace, where you can enjoy a light snack.

name: Ritzi Gourmet
review: Centrally located, close to the main train station and Zeppelin-Carré, this twin-track approach to dining awaits. In addition to its smart brasserie, Ritzi also boasts a fine dining counterpart. In this elegant restaurant – on a small gallery partially connected to the affiliated brasserie – Ben Benasr proposes a creative, modern set menu comprising up to six courses. Quality ingredients are used to create a cuisine that is rooted in French tradition but open to influences from further east – sophistication, finesse and depth of flavour abound. You can also expect accomplished service and expert wine advice.

name: Zur Tant
review: This well-maintained half-timbered house in an idyllic location on the Rhine has long been known as a hotspot for foodies. In 2014, Franz and Petra Hütter handed over the reins of their restaurant, which had been Michelin-starred for many years, to their head chef, Dresden-born Thomas Lösche. The classic setting is absolutely in keeping with the cuisine. The chef applies his precise culinary skill to select ingredients in order to concoct agreeably unfussy dishes. The stuffed quail served with celery, pear and grammel dumplings illustrates his ability to put craftsmanship and flavour centre stage. Choose from their fabulous selection of wines, many of which come from Austria. The view of the Rhine is wonderful, especially from the window seats and the terrace on the balcony!

name: Schwarzreiter
review: The legendary restaurant of Munich's Vier Jahreszeiten luxury hotel on the famous Maximilianstraße is definitely worth a visit! Here, a dedicated kitchen team cooks up "Young Bavarian Cuisine", which features modern, pared-down dishes that are prepared very meticulously and coherently. Only top-quality produce is used, preferably from the region. The chic interior is done out in a palette of soft cream tones and is both elegant and stylishly modern. The atmosphere is by no means stuffy, rather wonderfully sophisticated, and the front-of-house team is pleasantly relaxed and professional.

name: halbedel's Gasthaus
review: A well-to-do neighbourhood in Bad Godesberg, a Wilhelminian villa with a stylish yellow and white façade, an elegant interior with stucco, parquet flooring and modern touches – the perfect backdrop for Rainer-Maria Halbedel's cuisine. A legend of the German fine dining scene, he started cooking in 1966, received a Michelin star in 1984 at his former restaurant Korkeiche, and has held onto it ever since. He incorporates modern elements into his classic French cuisine and creates harmonious flavour combinations. Only the best produce is used, including eggs from his own hens and vegetables from his extensive garden in the Eifel. Opf for the "Menu Surprise" if you fancy the alternative vegetarian set menu. The handwritten wine list is very pleasing – the chef-patron will be happy to provide you with recommendations himself.

name: Sparkling Bistro
review: This pretty little bistro is slightly tucked away in the Amalienpassage, but it's worth seeking out for its excellent cuisine and appealing atmosphere. You need not fear an overly formal approach here; instead the ambience is pleasingly relaxed and straightforward. The courteous, genuine and friendly front-of-house team will also be able to give you excellent advice when it comes to wine. In the kitchen, owner Jürgen Wolfsgruber and Johannes Maria Kneip and their dedicated team deliver dishes that demonstrate a sensibility for subtle flavours and a well-thought-out structure that spotlights the excellent produce. In the evening, the food takes the form of a seven-course set menu.

name: Koch und Kellner
review: Your "Koch und Kellner" ("cook and waiter") here are head chef Gerald Hoffmann and maître d' and sommelier Frank Mackert. Not only does the latter ensure attentive service, but as a wine lover (he has a soft spot for Riesling), he uses his well-founded knowledge to recommend the perfect wine from a list of over 500 labels. "Rejuvenated classic" cuisine would be a fitting way to describe the food here. Excellent ingredients are pleasantly pared back and yet elaborately prepared. Written up on a blackboard, the set menu features dishes such as Franconian brook trout served with peas and a vin jaune sauce. A modern design of clear lines, a warm colour palette and parquet flooring makes for a lovely setting. By reservation only: Mon-Sat lunchtime (11.30am-2.30pm).

name: Apicius
review: The chic fine dining restaurant of the Jagdhaus Eiden has been run by the Zur Brügge family for generations. The ambience is wonderfully relaxed, which is largely down to the efficient, attentive and unflappable wait staff. A great setting for Tim Extra's cuisine, which is rooted in the classics but open to modern influences. He relies on high-quality regional produce, some of which comes from the restaurant's own garden or greenhouse. They also keep pigs and chickens and the locally sourced eel is smoked on site. It is clear in the way the five- or six-course set menu is presented how proud the kitchen team is of its selected ingredients. It is also worth mentioning the various snacks you can sample before your meal as well as the sweet treats to be had on the wonderfully well-stocked trolley of petits fours!

name: Jellyfish
review: If you're a fan of fish and seafood, then Jellyfish is the place for you. Come and sample the set menu, which is available in a longer or shorter version. You will also be able to order an excellent "exception" in the form of a meat or poultry dish. With the select ingredients being prepared in a considered, modern and creative way, the technical skill is second to none. As for the setting, the restaurant, located in the Schanzenviertel, has a pleasingly minimalist interior, all the better to focus on the interesting, polished cuisine. The experience is rounded out by the smart, attentive and knowledgeable young front-of-house team, who will also help you find your way around the wine list. Small bistro menu at lunchtime Sat-Sun.

name: Hofstube
review: They only offer one set menu here, and it is bursting with flavour, highly expressive and demonstrates meticulous craftsmanship. Having worked at award-winning establishments such as the Waldhotel Sonnora in Wittlich, La Vie in Osnabrück and Rüssel's Landhaus St Urban in Naurath (Wald), Felix Weber is now in charge of the kitchen at the Hofstube, where he creates modern seasonal cuisine. He has a fine nose for premium produce, which he sources from the region wherever possible. Skilled, friendly and attentive service and an attractive, high-quality setting complete the experience. Incidentally, the gourmet restaurant is part of Romantik- & Wellnesshotel Deimann – a manor house built in 1880 and owned by the Deimann family since 1917.

name: TAWA YAMA FINE
review: FINE is the name given to the stylish fine dining restaurant, which offers a creative set menu in the evening. Chef Peter Fridén – born in South Korea, raised in Sweden and influenced by French cuisine – skilfully combines classical, modern and Asian influences. There is also a vegetarian menu available. Alternatively, you can order à la carte. The extremely dedicated front-of-house team takes care of diners in a friendly and enjoyably unobtrusive manner, talking them through the menu in detail, while the sommelier helps with the wine selection. Incidentally, the Japanese name "TAWA YAMA" means "tower mountain" and is a reference to the Turmberg outside Karlsruhe. In addition to FINE, there is the trendy EASY, which has a simpler menu. You can use the hotel's own parking garage free of charge.

name: Le temple
review: Christiane Detemple-Schäfer and Oliver Schäfer form an absolute dream team. Your friendly hosts have been working side by side here since 1992 and their impressive dedication to the task has made Le temple a permanent fixture on the fine dining scene – not only in the small town of Neuhütten, but also among the Michelin-starred restaurants of Rhineland-Palatinate. This is a modern and creative take on classic cuisine – delicate, elaborate and extremely meticulous – to be enjoyed in the form of set menus, which change with the seasons. The interior of this elegant and minimalist restaurant is tastefully furnished, as is the small cigar lounge next door. If you want to spend a night amid the beautiful landscape of the Hunsrück, you can do so in cosy guestrooms – a delicious breakfast is also available.

name: Admiral
review: High-quality food that represents excellent value for money! An institution in the region, this is a truly charming restaurant to which your dedicated hosts have brought a touch of originality. In the kitchen, chef-patron Holger Stehr cooks up an interesting mix of modern and classic fare. His expressive creations demonstrate real depth of flavour and are also beautifully presented. You are welcomed by Martina Kraemer-Stehr, a trained sommelier, who is responsible for the friendly and well-drilled service. The wine list and recommendations never fail to impress. The wines by the glass, available as pairings to both of the set menus, take diners on a stimulating wine tour. Tip: try to bag the pretty guestroom in the charming sandstone pavilion in the Admiral Garden.

name: ZweiSinn Meiers | Fine Dining
review: This stylish, modern restaurant just outside Nuremberg's city centre is a welcome addition to the fine dining scene in the Franconian metropolis. Following stints working at first-class establishments such as Louis C. Jacob in Hamburg, Amador in Langen, and under Johanna Maier in Filzmoos, Austria, Stefan Meier struck out on his own a few years ago. Together with a motivated kitchen team, he combines the finest hand-selected ingredients to create imaginative dishes brimming with beautifully balanced flavours. Vegetarians are also catered for. Last but not least, the professional, friendly and attentive service also contributes to the feel-good atmosphere in this chic, minimalist-style restaurant.

name: SEO Küchenhandwerk
review: The small restaurant in the Seevital Hotel exudes a sense of exclusivity. Done out in a smart and sophisticated style, it has just a handful of tables. It stands a stone's throw from the water and boasts a fabulous terrace with wonderful views of the lake and mountains. Roland Pieber's intensely flavoursome cuisine is no less noteworthy. Using first-rate ingredients, the young Austrian chef has a very ambitious, creative and modern approach to cooking. The kitchen team also serve and explain the dishes of the eight-course surprise menu. Expert wine recommendations are also provided by the friendly staff.

name: Anthony's Kitchen
review: Your host Anthony Sarpong runs what turns out to be an appealing mix of restaurant and cookery school. Heading up a highly dedicated team, this Ghanaian-born chef delivers innovative international cuisine scattered with seasonal influences. There are two set menus on offer: "The Expedition" and the vegetarian "Green Journey" – each comprising well-thought-out creations incorporating interesting combinations of flavours and select ingredients. The dishes are in keeping with the spirit of the times, as is the smart decor and informal atmosphere, with the chefs occasionally delivering dishes to diners themselves. Incidentally, the restaurant is certified organic and attaches great importance to sustainability.

name: der Schneider
review: Modern and fuss-free fine dining, just the way we like it! This applies as much to the cuisine as it does to the setting. The restaurant in the Hotel Ambiente, which is located in the Wambel district, proposes a pleasingly trendy and informal atmosphere (check out the two dining pods – perfect for couples!), although in summer you may well prefer the sheltered terrace to the rear. The man at the helm is Phillip Schneider, who delivers modern and innovative cuisine that is full of flavour contrasts yet beautifully balanced. His dishes are presented to diners in the form of two "customised" set menus. One is completely vegetarian, the other showcases carefully sourced meat and fish. You can also dine à la carte. Courteous and competent service, excellent wine recommendations.

name: Storstad
review: "Storstad" means "big city" and refers to the chef's time in Stockholm. But it's not just the name that's Swedish here – you will also find Nordic touches in the decor and cuisine of this chic urban restaurant on the fifth floor of the Turmtheater. Up here in the historical Goliath House, you can also make the most of the wonderful terrace with its views of the cathedral. Chef-patron Anton Schmaus can depend on his dedicated and talented kitchen team. Under the direction of head chef Josef Weig, they deliver creative dishes that can be sampled in the form of either the regular or vegetarian set menu. The excellent food is accompanied by beautifully paired wines and served by an accomplished, courteous front-of-house team. At lunchtime, there is a smaller set menu as well as an excerpt from the evening menu.

name: Jean
review: In addition to its hotel and café, the Frankenbach family also runs Jean in this former wine bar. After working in renowned establishments such as Ikarus in Salzburg and Restaurant Heinz Winkler in Aschau, Johannes Frankenbach (the third generation of the family) has been at the helm here since 2012. Even the name "Jean" (a French equivalent of Johannes) is a nod to his love of France, which is as much a part of his ingredient-led, Mediterranean-influenced cuisine as is his knack for creating fine aromas and flavour contrasts. This is accompanied by judicious and fairly priced wine pairings. The setting is also charming: half-height wooden panelling, elegant table settings, old photos... while outside is the pretty plane tree courtyard. The young lady of the house waits on diners in a pleasingly friendly and down-to-earth fashion.

name: Handwerk
review: An upscale, trendy and minimalist design, outstanding creative modern dishes, and informal yet competent service – this restaurant meets the brief of "Casual.Fine.Dining". This place is aptly named, in that craftsmanship ("Handwerk") plays a major role in the open kitchen. Head chef Thomas Wohlfeld combines it with his own original ideas, drawing on North German tradition and subtle Far Eastern influences. Minimalist and ingredient-led dishes such as Vierländer Platte tomatoes with melon and Belper Knolle or cod with raspberry and almond are available in the form of a set menu of five or six courses (seven on request) – and at a reasonable price. The wine pairings are just right. There is a lovely terrace in the front garden.

name: Gasthaus zum Raben
review: Many guests who visit the charming farmhouse from 1728 for the first time will think of an old picture postcard from a bygone era – that's how idyllic this place looks. Inside, painted wooden ceilings, rustic wooden tables and benches and an old tiled stove make for a cosy atmosphere. In addition, owner Steffen Disch and his team serve up excellent cuisine. The classic French dishes are based on regional produce and cleverly incorporate international influences. You can also enjoy the benefits of Horben spring water. Those who would like to stay a little longer and enjoy the wonderful Black Forest landscape can spend the night in one of the attractive, comfortable guestrooms of the charming inn.

name: San Martino - Gourmet by Jochen Fecht
review: Head down into the basement of this townhouse located in the heart of Constance to sample a creative set menu put together by chef-patron Jochen Fecht. Diners take their seats in an elegant and minimalist setting that makes a feature of its distinctive natural stone walls. You can then look forward to a modern take on classic cuisine that draws on first-rate ingredients to deliver flavoursome dishes that pack a punch. Peruse the menu – the dishes such as turbot fillet and king salmon with orange beech smoke, quinoa, grapefruit, coriander and capers are enough to make your mouth water! Friendly and professional service.

name: MAIN TOWER Restaurant & Lounge
review: A great location in the heart of Frankfurt. Take the lift up to the 53rd floor and bag a table by the window to experience a view you don't often get to enjoy – the panorama over the rooftops of "Mainhatten" is downright spectacular! The cuisine is equally impressive – to be sampled in the form of a set menu comprising four to seven courses. Not only are the dishes visually appealing, they are also delicious, drawing on high-quality ingredients in their elegant combinations of Asian flavours. There is also a vegetarian alternative. You can sip an aperitif in the lounge before dinner (from 9pm you are also welcome just for drinks). A reservation gets you a free ticket for the lift and also grants you access to the observation deck.

name: BjörnsOX
review: Björn Leist proposes a single-menu concept that expresses his affinity with his homeland of the Rhön Mountains. Using first-rate, mostly regional ingredients, he concocts a creative, no-frills "surprise menu". The restaurant is proud to breed its own pasture-raised oxen, a sentiment that is reflected on the plate. The high-quality meat and other excellent produce can sometimes be found in several variations in a single dish – this is cuisine to be savoured! Diners are seated in a quaint little dining space; the wood panelling and timberwork lend it a wonderfully cosy atmosphere, along with the banquette seating on all sides and snug recesses. Next door, the SaxenHof hotel proposes cheerful modern guestrooms, while WohnZimmer serves alternative culinary options.

name: Mountain Hub Gourmet
review: Not far from the airport, the fine dining restaurant of the Hilton Munich Airport Hotel draws guests in with the fantastic cuisine of Stefan Barnhusen, who has already made a name for himself thanks to his Michelin-starred cuisine in Hamburg's Jellyfish. He uses outstanding ingredients and his own refined sense of inspiration to come up with creative combinations of remarkably intense flavours. These come in the form of an interesting set menu comprising up to seven courses – with wine pairings if desired. The attentive and friendly service team is headed up by maître d' Johannes J. Gahberger. With its semi-circular floor plan, the restaurant itself is spacious and boasts a chic modern design.

name: Casala
review: It is quite something to sit on the terrace in fine weather and look out over Lake Constance! Add the Michelin-starred cuisine and diners couldn't ask for more… Dedicated owners Manfred and Susanne Lang are able to offer this fine dining experience thanks to head chef Markus Philippi, whose creations are modern and seasonal. One of the many well-balanced and flavourful dishes he puts together is the Hohentwiel water buffalo served with a wonderful roasted onion jus, potato soufflé and garden vegetables. The smart, upmarket interior is perfectly in line with the sophisticated food, as is the extremely obliging, friendly and competent front-of-house team. The experienced sommelier with his excellent wine suggestions completes the picture.

name: Entenstuben
review: His dream was to have his own restaurant, and this dream has come true for Fabian Denninger. After working at the two-star restaurant Edsbacka Krog in Sollentuna near Stockholm, at Burg Wernberg and at Waldhotel Sonnora in Wittlich, the Mannheim-born chef went on to head up the kitchen of Koch und Kellner here in Nuremberg, before becoming the owner and head chef of Entenstuben in June 2014. His dishes are anchored in the classics, rely on good, fresh produce and show the chef's penchant for acidic contrasts. There are two set menus, one of which is vegetarian. In addition to the fabulous presentation, the restaurant itself is also a sight to behold: minimalist and at the same time cosy.

name: Showroom
review: The name "Showroom" hits the nail on the head – this is indeed where head chef Dominik Käppeler presents the whole range of his culinary creativity. Diners are treated to a set menu composed of five to eight courses, and a surprise menu at that. You just choose the number of courses and mention any ingredients you don't like – the rest is up to the kitchen team. Top-notch produce (they are proud of their Bavarian Wagyu beef, for example) is used to conjure up modern dishes brimming with innovation; occasionally they demonstrate a playful touch or unusual flavour combinations. Urban ambience and friendly and attentive service – interesting wine recommendations. The chef also likes to come to the table and explain the concept behind the menu.

name: Schloss Filseck
review: Not only is Schloss Filseck a museum, cultural centre and venue for events, it is also a hotspot for foodies! A tasteful, modern ambience prevails in the restaurant, while the wooden ceiling and quarry stone walls add an old-fashioned, rustic charm to proceedings. There is also a wonderful terrace laid out in the interior courtyard. The cuisine clearly draws much of its inspiration from Italy and elsewhere in the Mediterranean, and head chef Daniele Corona delivers coherent and technically precise dishes for the evening's fine dining set menu. A vegetarian alternative is also proposed. You can expect expert advice when choosing from the well-put-together wine list. An inexpensive lunch menu is available. Highly practical: Free shuttle service within a 20km radius of the castle.

name: Anima
review: On the ground floor of a modern building, the minimalist-style dining space offers a view of the outside through floor-to-ceiling windows – only a hedge separates you from the Danube. In the open kitchen, chef Heiko Lacher expresses his personality – this also explains the name "Anima" (the Latin word for "soul"). His style is a creative and equally harmonious combination of different culinary cultures, not least French and Italian. Working with excellent produce, beautiful flavour combinations are achieved, to which home-grown herbs also contribute. Oysters or caviar are available as an optional addition to the set menu.

name: Rebers Pflug
review: As soon as you enter the restaurant, you will pass the open kitchen, which is sure to whet your appetite. The menu is really wide-ranging, from regional classics such as Tafelspitz or Rostbraten, to the "Genießer-Menü", which comes in three to six courses. A vegetarian alternative is also available. And then there are the prized steaks! Naturally, chef-patron Hans-Harald Reber gets his excellent meat from his trusted butcher, who happens to be a second cousin of his. You can soak up the friendly and pleasantly informal atmosphere, safe in the knowledge you will be looked after attentively by the proficient front-of-house team. Plus: you have the option of booking one of the comfortable guestrooms.

name: Kesselhaus
review: Once a venue for events and parties, this distinctive building on the industrial estate is now a cool location for Michelin-starred cuisine. This attractive space rocks an industrial look: out front, there is a lovely terrace next to a striking brick chimney; inside, a loft atmosphere reigns. Diners sit beneath high ceilings, surrounded by exposed brick walls, tall mullioned windows and chic design features such as the solid wood "Center Table" and comic art on the walls. As modern and creative dishes are being prepared by Randy de Jong and his team, restaurant manager and owner Thayarni Garthoff provides professional service in a relaxed atmosphere. There are also two gorgeous lounges, one of which affords a view into the glass-fronted kitchen. Lunch is also available on Saturdays.

name: Eisenbahn
review: The experience and ideas of two generations are to be found in the Wolf family establishment. This is also true of the food in this restaurant, which has held a Michelin star since 1997. It draws inspiration from both classic cooking and modern, international cuisine. Diners can expect choice ingredients, delicate aromas and an intense hit of flavour. This is a kitchen that focuses on the essentials and eschews frills. The dishes are served in the form of a seasonal set menu, available in a varying number of courses. In addition to the excellent culinary fare, you can look forward to cordial and professional service. The tasteful interior and the pretty terrace behind the house are also inviting. And there is a fabulous international selection of wines. The Bistro s'Bähnle provides more dining options. You can also stay overnight.

name: FAVORITE restaurant
review: Located in Mainz's city park and run by the dedicated Barth family, Favorite Parkhotel is not only a sophisticated place to stay but its fine dining restaurant is a popular destination in its own right. The owners made the right call in hiring head chef Tobias Schmitt, previously sous-chef at Frankfurt's Lafleur. His modern cuisine draws on excellent produce to conjure up streamlined and coherent dishes. The set menus on offer are called "Roots" ("The roots of cooking") and "Blossom" ("Light, modern & contemporary cuisine"), and there is also a vegetarian alternative. As for the restaurant itself, it boasts a refined and elegant interior. A table by the window is your best bet – or dine on the beautiful terrace overlooking the Rhine and Taunus.

name: Das Marktrestaurant
review: Much to the delight of his guests, Andreas Hillejan, originally from the Lower Rhine, moved to Upper Bavaria some years ago. Here in the beautiful village of Mittenwald, at the foot of the Karwendel Mountains, he offers his own refined take on traditional pub cuisine, resulting in some really crowd-pleasing dishes. Take a seat in the pleasingly informal, simple dining room and opt for the "Wirtshaus mal anders" set menu or one of the appealing à la carte dishes. Before or after your meal, you might like to take a walk through the colourfully painted houses of this pretty historical town, which is renowned for its violin makers and climatic health resort – you won't have far to go, as the restaurant is very close to the pedestrianised zone.

name: Weinsinn
review: You'll need to ring the bell to gain access to this restaurant in the lively and bustling Bahnhofsviertel. The interior is exceedingly chic: a large, bright, high-ceilinged space done out in a minimalist, urban style – decorative works of art add appealing points of interest. From almost anywhere in the room you can watch the chefs in the open kitchen as they go about their work, conjuring up modern, creative dishes out of choice ingredients. Jochim Busch, head chef at Gustav (this is its sister restaurant), and sous-chef Daniel Pletsch are at the helm here. Guests can expect friendly and accomplished service from the attentive and well-organised front-of-house team, which includes a sommelier who can recommend nice wines by the glass to accompany the large or small set menu. A word to the wise: Be sure to stop off for an aperitif or digestif in the charming garden to the rear of the house.

name: Ursprung
review: Andreas and Anna Widmann (the eighth generation of the family to run this place) have two restaurants, and this is the fine dining option. It is a compact restaurant with a rather intimate atmosphere, located in the oldest part of Widmann's Löwen, where the village butcher's shop used to be. The chic, plush decor comprises a mix of modern lines and warm wood, which establishes a connection to the region… a connection that continues on the menu, where Swabian tradition meets sophisticated culinary skill.
