A small pleasant outdoor space in the inner courtyard and excellent value for money complete the picture.

name: Tač
review: Despite its location in a residential district outside the city centre, it’s worth heading off the beaten track to eat in this restaurant with its welcoming dining rooms and attractive summer terrace. Meat and fish dishes feature on the menu – we particularly enjoyed the fish, which is of a very high quality and prepared in simple, traditional recipes.

name: Vuglec Breg
review: Housed in a rural hillside property in a secluded panoramic location, this restaurant serves traditional, regional cuisine using home-produced (including the wine) or locally sourced ingredients which are full of authentic flavour. Roast meats are one of the specialities on the menu, while the attractive wine cellar is worth a visit.

name: Izakaya by Time
review: It’s worth walking a little further away from the town centre to get to this modern restaurant, which serves mainly Japanese cuisine with the occasional Croatian influence. The dining room is dominated by a large cocktail bar, while an attractive outdoor terrace offers a peaceful, relaxing ambience. In true Croatian tradition, the tempting dessert trolley is a real must.

name: Bait Maryam
review: Named after the owner’s mother, this passionately run ‘home’ offers a warm welcome and delicious, home-style Levantine dishes cooked with love. Sit in the cool, tranquil dining room or out on the glass-enclosed lakeside terrace. The lunch ‘dish of the day & soup’ is a steal – and dessert is a must.

name: Goldfish
review: Vibrant, modern Japanese dishes – from sushi, uni and yakitori to sharing plates and Wagyu steak – are the order of the day at this funky, buzzing spot located in a smart mall. Prices are more than reasonable, and service is bright and keen; sit at the counter to watch the chefs at work.

name: Ibn Albahr
review: This Lebanese seafood restaurant features fishing paraphernalia like ropes, anchors and even a boat – as well as a beautiful terrace with a great view of the beach. Head to the fresh fish counter to choose what you’d like to eat; simple yet delicious dishes let the ingredients speak for themselves.

name: folly
review: Tucked away in Souk Madinat, this popular restaurant features an outside terrace and bar as well as a kitchen counter where you can watch the chefs in action. The ingredient-led menu offers precise, modern dishes which are pared-back in style, with an appealing clarity of flavour. Staff are warm and engaging.

name: Ninive
review: It’s set in a bustling area of the city, but this charming restaurant exists in another world: a relaxing oasis, a step back in time. The design reflects a Bedouin tent, with rugs and lanterns, low tables and cosy sofas. Tasty, well-priced dishes come from all over the Middle East and North Africa.

name: Michael's Genuine
review:
This Design District pioneer from Chef Michael Schwartz is as popular now as it was when it first debuted almost 15 years ago. A well-heeled crowd flocks here, but whether it's a requisite respite from boutique hopping, a spot to catch up with friends or a meal to close a business deal, this dining delight is for everyone. The courtyard is a lovely place to linger, thanks to its lush greenery, fans and heat lamps (when necessary). The interior space features concrete flooring and an inviting bar. A jazz playlist adds to the upbeat and conversation-filled air.
The menu focuses on unfussy yet skillful cooking. Staples like pizza, house-made pasta, crudo, pan-roasted chicken and wood oven-roasted fish keep fans returning time and time again.

name: El Turco
review:
This charming café, sheltered within a shopping enclave, hosts a loyal following at outdoor tables shaded by age-old oak trees. Inside, Chef Vural Aydoğan and team work out of a glass-walled kiosk, dressed up with blue-and-white tile as well as neatly lined cans and bottles.
The menu is an enticing offering of breakfast fare, featuring organic eggs that support Turkish mezzes, manti and savory pastries like borek. Baked in-house, this burnished coil is stuffed with spinach, sprinkled with sesame seeds and garnished with cherry tomatoes. The izmir kofte arrives in a mini ceramic dish filled with beef meatballs baked in tomato sauce alongside batons of roasted potato. A single charred jalapeño adds the perfect bit of heat to each mouthful.

name: Mandolin Aegean Bistro
review:
Founded by husband and wife, Ahmet Erkaya and Anastasia Koutsioukis, this charming bistro welcomes diners with a blue door and whitewashed façade. The space features wood tables, lacquered chairs and an outdoor bar, although the focus is on its courtyard dining area, enhanced with mature trees, orchids and electric fans. This mezze-heavy menu may unveil a creamy slab of baked feta with diced tomato, smoked chili flakes and Turkish peppers. Slices of house-baked bread, stuffed into small brown paper bags, accompany the excellent small plates. Salads, a grilled catch-of-the-day sandwich and larger items, like moussaka, are equally beloved.
A wedge of honey pie with a salted shortbread crust is highly recommended, and pairs delightfully with that Turkish coffee.

name: Swine & Sons
review:
From well-known local husband-and-wife duo, Rhys and Alexia Gawlak, arrives this sandwich concept nestled within the Local Butcher shop and market. There is seating both outside (on the festive patio) as well as inside in the multi-concept space, furnished with wood tables, metal chairs and that infamous counter all the way in the back.
The menu is as compact as the room itself and once your food is presented, it's hard to focus on much else. The fried chicken sandwich with pimento cheese, bacon and varying sauces to match is a signature for good reason, while a side of German potato salad boasts just as much boldness in flavor and seasoning. A simple-sounding but perfectly executed oatmeal cookie sandwich with buttercream ends the meal on a joyful note.

name: Bachour
review:
Open since 2019, an arch of roses marks the entrance to this airy and inviting bijou. A perch at the counter in the back offers diners a front-row view of the glass-enclosed bakery (and bakers in action). While the ambience is appealingly industrial and spartan with exposed ductwork, cement floors and natural hues, those shelves of brightly colored tarts and pastries form the focus of the space.
A meal here may commence with ham croquettes and garlic aïoli; tailed by a seafood causa salad with aji amarillo-infused potato purée. When hankering for pasta, there's no going wrong with fettucine pomodoro. Be sure to take home a box or two of their wonderful sweets, like the mango-passion fruit macarons or a slice of lemon pie.

name: Zak The Baker
review:
This all-day operation is the brainchild of self-taught baker Zak Stern. He grew up in Miami, then apprenticed at a number of organic farms in Sweden, France and Israel before returning to his hometown to fulfill his culinary dreams. The crux of his menu is baked, as in breads and pastries, along with sandwiches, soups and salads. The "BLT" features salmon bacon, lettuce and tomato all stuffed into a deliciously flaky croissant. For something sweet, get the flourless dark chocolate cookie bursting with whole toasted almonds.
This kosher bakery and café is located in hip Wynwood and welcomes diners with a color-splashed façade. Its breakfast and lunch hours are supplemented by an evening falafel service, so come and be ready to stay.

name: Rooster and the Till
review:
It's a low-key spot with simple décor and a large image of the eponymous fowl. The bar is central and wraps around an open kitchen, so grab a seat at the counter for the best view. Between the lively tunes and buzzy staff, the aura is anything but stuffy. The plates follow suit—freewheeling, frequently changing and shareable with elements from SE Asia, Latin America and the Levant. Yet, nothing seems out of place, as in sumac-flecked cauliflower with whipped goat's milk feta and falafel-spiced dukkah. Fried cobia collar with nuoc cham boasts a cultish following.
Such seductive textures and explosive flavors continue in full force in a dessert of black sesame ice cream with pineapple-cashew jam and Thai tea caramel.

name: Domu
review:
Enter Chef/owner Sean "Sonny" Nguyen's trendy ramen haven and you'll find two rooms dressed with concrete floors, a marble bar and wood panels set aglow by a starburst light fixture. The second room cradles the bulk of the crowd. As the name illustrates, this chef makes his culinary "dreams come true" by dint of a classic-meets-creative menu. Beyond the small plates lies the star item—ramen. Creations, like the Ritchie Rich and Curry, are full of bold, memorable flavors and certainly worth a slurp. Tokyo ramen with shoyu chicken broth, fried chicken thigh and duck fat is a sensory feat. Couple it with blistered shishitos for a delicious touch—and bit of crunch.
It's all in the family here as sib Tori Tori flaunts a similarly creative izakaya menu.

name: Ichicoro Ramen
review:
The vibe inside this stylish den has a cool, underground edge but hungry noodle seekers need only look for a prominent bowl-shaped, black-and-yellow sign, which glows like a beacon at night. A snack of crunchy, house-made chicharrónes dusted with ichimi pepper is a nice way to whet the appetite, but ramen remains the main draw. Expect finely tuned bowls with enticingly springy noodles; savory, full-bodied broths based on chicken or pork (or both); and accoutrements that show a bit of personality, as in pork belly chasyu asado or grilled Gulf shrimp. For a hit of extra spice, turn to sauces like the tantalizing jalapeño-yuzu kosho.
Peak business hours can see substantial wait times, so do call ahead to secure a place in line.

name: Bombay Street Kitchen
review:
Amit Kumar's fresh and fine outlet sports a welcoming exterior and cheerful interior, done up with orange booths and bright accents. Diners may settle in for a range of enjoyable, well-prepared South Indian small plates which form the nucleus of this tempting menu.
The street special dosa is a departure from the norm, here stuffed with potato, cabbage, paneer and red onion, and served with coconut sambal and curry gravy for dipping.
Vegetarians will thrill to the sight of meat-free specials, like kathal masaledar, featuring tender chunks of jackfruit in a zesty tomato-and-onion masala; while tandoor options like hara teekha murg tikka (skewers of white meat chicken marinated in a herbal mixture) is grilled to luscious, crisp perfection.

name: DOYA
review:
This Wynwood operation is particularly beloved, thanks to its lush patio. Inside, the room is vast, open, light-filled and designed with every type of diner in mind. Seats facing the open kitchen offer an intimate experience, while couples may prefer tables armed with powder-blue velvet chairs for a bit of romance.
The cuisine bills itself as modern Aegean, and you will discover elements from Greece and Turkey’s coastal regions. Nibble on a refreshing fig salad with greens tossed in a hazelnut-pomegranate dressing before moving on to sea beans with garlic yogurt or some of the most delicate manti in this part of town. Flavors are both correct and comforting, but a scoop of raki ice cream will leave you supremely happy.

name: Strand
review:
Husband-and-wife duo Alda and Joe Rees are behind this corner spot nestled within an Art Deco building. Its menu, displayed on the front windows, invites passersby inside to a space that may be short on real estate but utterly captivates with mint-green walls and Mason jars that hang above the glossy tiled bar.
The seasonal American menu brims with nostalgic Southern inspiration, and presentations are dialed back to let ingredients shine. From local tomatoes to fresh citrus, dishes exude a homey sense. To wit: chilled shrimp is a wonderful contrast against hot fried green tomatoes, while cobia with mustard sauce and Carolina gold rice requires little augmentation. Close out with a citrus olive oil cake along with a sip from the worthy wine list.

name: The Ravenous Pig
review:
This Winter Park modern gastropub came to be thanks to the vision of noted restaurateurs, James and Julie Petrakis. Housed right beside their eponymous brewery, the space exudes a moody, industrial vibe by way of charcoal hues, rustic wood accents and a gray ceiling marked by exposed ductwork. The open kitchen on the left has frosted glass panels that add a bit of mystery to the culinary proceedings.
Chef Clay Miller's menu is a bona fide study of classic pub fare with creative Southern spins—to wit, ranchero sauce-dressed pork burnt ends over cornbread pudding or cured pastrami brisket with pickled cabbage purée and cauliflower giardiniera. The vegetable-forward melon, cucumber and farmer's cheese combo is in fact a rather complex denouement.

name: Z Asian
review:
Simple on the outside, this casual gem is beloved for its distinctively bold dishes and thoughtful design. As you enter, you'll notice their name emblazoned on a black wall. Other stylish details include hanging lanterns, ceiling fans and artwork throughout. The aura is Southeast Asian, not unlike the focused Vietnamese cooking.
Dishes are flavorful, bursting with nuance and balance. Behold the simple yet sublime dia nho like sautéed bok choy with crispy garlic; and bánh xèo, fried crêpe with shrimp, thinly sliced pork and a tangy fish sauce. Phở tái brings nostalgia to the forefront with that classic beef broth, afloat with rice noodles, eye of round steak and scallions. Donning a host of aromatics (bean sprouts, lime and jalapeño), it is a riot of flavor.

name: Phuc Yea
review:
There is nothing subtle about Chef Cesar Zapata and Ani Meinhold’s raucous Vietnamese mash-up in the MiMo district. A concrete compound wrapped in glowing red lanterns, the restaurant is practically a club with its sultry lighting, cavernous interior and full-time DJ. Yet, none of it gets in the way of the food, which is boldly seasoned and generously portioned. Stacks of crispy imperial rolls wrapped with mint and tangles of garlic-butter egg noodles aggressively charred on a wok are solid starting points. Everything is meant to be shared, especially the pho, which arrives in a cauldron packed with herbs, rice noodles and a meltingly tender slab of hickory-smoked short rib.
All the while, a nearby table might launch into song. You are welcome to join the fun.

name: Papa Llama
review:
For a Peruvian menu that's diverse in its brevity, this is your spot. Don't be fooled by its modest surrounds, as the space, featuring white walls, a black ceiling and warm wood tones, is modern and cool. Leather chairs are especially inviting and tables offer a view of the gleaming kitchen. Come with a crowd to make the most of this shareable menu, full of bright, approachable ingredients given the depth of flavor treatment. Start with the papa rellenas, or ground sirloin croquettes served with a jammy egg. Arroz chaufa with aji panca chicken is an ace take on Chinese fried rice; while picarones, sweet potato-doughnuts with clove honey, make for a fine way to finish your meal.
The wine list is solid, but beers (listed by style) take the cake.

name: La Natural
review:
You wouldn’t think to make reservations for a pizza place in Little River, but think again. The crowds can be relentless at this popular hangout, which feels rather like an underground party by way of concrete floors and dim lighting.
Creative toppings like za’atar and Sichuan peppercorns sing on stunning, picture-perfect pies zealously charred in a wood-burning oven hiding behind the bar. We’re partial to the classic burrata and basil pie, which arrives puffy and pillowy thanks to the signature crust that's cold-fermented for 48 hours. An astute selection of starters (try the papaya with kumquat) and one of the city’s longest lists for natural wines only add to the appeal of this essential pizzeria. A personable staff keeps a close watch on every table.

name: Zitz Sum
review:
There are countless rules and traditions when it comes to cooking, but don’t tell Pablo Zitzmann, whose inspiration stretches from China to Japan to Italy. Following the wild success of his dumpling pop-up, the Colombian chef found a home on the ground floor of an admittedly stoic office building in Coral Gables. It is the last place you would expect to find crispy pork pot stickers with Calabrian chili oil and fried garlic, or a thick wedge of charred cabbage capped with melted parmesan cheese and set in a pool of Fresno chili butter.
The cooking is original and gutsy; and plates like the shrimp har gow with lime and a tamarind-black garlic chutney exemplify a kind of fearless, borderless ethos that, in the end, makes delicious sense.

name: Red Rooster Overtown
review:
Overtown is a neighborhood rich with art, history and culture. Fittingly, this vibrant dining room celebrates it all through its food. Decorative elements, like a horseshoe-shaped bar, Moroccan tiles and leafy plants, convey a tropical feel; while sculptures curated by the Pérez Art Museum in Miami are an art historian's dream.
Chef Tristen Epps is of Trinidadian background and puts his own unique stamp on the cooking of Chef Marcus Samuelsson's enticing concept. The results are extraordinary - Wagyu oxtail, anyone? He might then take chicken and waffles on a spin with crispy yard bird, while the spice-rubbed avocado toast elevates the American standby to inventive heights. Cookies and cream cake, with buttercream and Oreos, is indulgence epitomized.

name: Hometown Barbecue Miami
review:
From Austin, Texas to Brooklyn, New York, Pitmaster Bill Durney brings his signature barbecue to Magic City. Just like the original location, Durney has built this warehouse-chic space amidst a sea of industry in the Miami Produce Center, where trucks and moving pallets roam the streets. The sheer scale of the space—open kitchen on one side, a long bar on the other, tables in between and a patio just beyond—is something to behold.
A hulking beef rib crusted with salt and black pepper, as well as melting, charred slices of brisket are essential orders that have few equals outside of Texas. Satisfying sides, like Frito pie, plancha broccoli and charred summer corn, round out the meal. The food here arrives almost as quickly as it’s ordered, so come hungry.

name: Lung Yai Thai Tapas
review:
You could drive down the street a dozen times and still overlook this intimate little nook that hides in plain sight. Little Havana is certainly an unexpected place to find one of the city’s hottest Thai kitchens, but if the long waits are any indication, Chef/owner Veenuthri Trisransri knows what he’s doing. On a menu that mixes typical standbys with Northern specialties, start with the excellent grilled beef salad or crispy duck salad. Sinus-clearing heat builds in a fiery larb muang aggressively seasoned with cumin, chilies and star anise; while khao soi is a bowl of comforting yellow curry.
Tables, plates and even the place itself is small, so order ambitiously and be prepared for a kitchen that sends out dishes faster than you can finish them.

name: Rocca
review:
Chef Bryce Bonsack's culinary background includes experience in cutting-edge kitchens in New York as well as training in regional Italian cooking (the name is an homage to the Piedmontese family that took him under their wing). He demonstrates both skill sets to great effect in this hip, of-the-moment eatery.
Naturally, there's an assortment of pastas, skillfully made in house, which showcase classic flavors and scrupulous technique, like supple tagliolini with beef ragù and 30-month-aged Parmigiano. Guests ooh and ahh over mozzarella hand pulled to order in a tableside cart, but the flavor outshines the show. Perhaps most exciting of all are the displays of originality, as in a vibrant hiramasa carpaccio with green apple, capers and horseradish.

name: Ghee Indian Kitchen
review:
In the thick of a shopping mall, find Niven Patel’s smash-hit restaurant. Warehouse floors, mango wood tables and a wall lined with rows upon rows of spice jars are bound to put diners in the mood for the team's smartly spiced food.
The kitchen takes no cues from its suburban locale; in fact, it features a tight menu of flavor-packed dishes made with ingredients sourced from Chef Patel’s own farm. Ghost pepper-cheddar seed naan is a fiery, puff-pastry-like riff, while yellowfin tuna bhel with avocado makes for a zesty first course. Kerala lamb with tomato and coconut is a richly satisfying effort with layered notes, soft basmati rice and meltingly tender meat.

name: Lucali
review:
Although it's located in sunny South Beach, Lucali exudes a charming rusticity that calls to mind its original Brooklyn locale. The greenery-adorned, umbrella-shaped sidewalk is ultra-tempting; or beat the heat and find a seat inside—outfitted with plank floors and chunky tables. The wood-fired brick oven at the rear is sure to stoke the appetite. The 20-inch pizza is lusciously charred and sports a light crust crowned with fresh pomodoro sauce, a combination of cheeses and fragrant sprigs of basil. Various toppings are offered to embellish the pie, and one may even choose to have just half dressed with say, meatball crumbles and green chili slivers. 
The bar, which opens in the evening, offers diners the option of a 12-inch pie.

name: Itamae
review:
In a city teeming with high quality fish and designer brands, this Peruvian restaurant might be one of the best perches to make the most of both. Located in the Miami Design Center, the family-run, Nikkei-inspired Itamae started out as a simple counter in 2018 before relocating to the ground floor of an open-air court.
A clever, curated selection of bright, electrifying cebiches, colorful tiraditos and creative maki dazzle in full view of stores like Van Cleef and Hublot. Cooked dishes are just as impressive, like tender swordfish served with sweet Murasaki potatoes and sarza criolla, or conchitas à la parmesana, a bold combination of Hokkaido scallops resting atop avocado rolls, blanketed in bubbling parmesan and finished with lime.

name: Krüs Kitchen
review:
This airy, glass-fronted operation blends in with the rest of its cool neighbors in the heart of bustling Coconut Grove. But take a closer look: at night, Chef Sebastián Vargas’s dinner-only Los Felix is in full swing; by day, the breezy space becomes Krüs Kitchen, home to creative bowls, salads and sandwiches.
Truly, the likes of wild-caught Florida shrimp, sweet lump crab meat and smoked, grass-fed pastrami elevate an all-day everyday, chef-driven menu that has broad appeal. Part kitchen and part retail market, the second floor also highlights small, organic and biodynamic producers and other curated goods. As an added bonus, a percentage of sales benefits the group’s nonprofit arm that aims to serve future community needs.

name: Chug's Diner
review:
What started out as a small café has grown overnight into this full-scale, Coconut Grove essential. All credit is due to Chef Michael Beltran who runs this terrific Cuban diner, fitted with dangling greenery and cozy booths. Truly, if this kitchen were a car, it would break the speed limit, as the team hurries about—opening early, closing late and cooking with panache.
One could make a meal out of the oxtail ajiaco alone, a satisfying Colombian stew that cures all ills. But then you wouldn’t have room for the several towering sandwiches, served on fluffy Cuban bread. No meal is complete without at least one of their guava- and cream-cheese pastelitos. Their warm, flaky pastry alone will guarantee a return visit.

name: Tinta y Cafe
review:
Coral Gables is home to this original operation, happily christened with a name that translates to ink and coffee. Unsurprisingly, there are artfully arranged bookshelves that line its glass façade, while the interior design most certainly resembles that of a coffee shop. Guests may order at the window, grab a table either inside or out under a cluster of palm trees, and settle in for a litany of Cuban delicacies.
The furniture is mid-century modern, but the sandwich-focused menu is as classic and comforting as ever. Deep-fried croquetas are not to be missed; and the pavo real with turkey and cream cheese is nothing if not satisfying. Our allegiance, however, is with the patria (their take on the Cubano with pork, ham, mustard and pickles.)

name: Sanguich De Miami
review:
What started out as a little shipping container in 2017 has morphed into this brick-and-mortar hot spot in Little Havana. There is almost always a line of diners vying to squeeze into the narrow space, designed with emerald-green walls, vibrant tile and sleek brass trimmings.
Everyone comes for the same thing: a superb Cuban sandwich featuring pork butt that's been marinated for a week in garlic and spices, then pressed between expertly grilled slices of house-made bread. A heavier but equally flavorful alternative is the lechon, starring tender shredded pork slathered in garlic-cilantro aïoli. Thick baton-shaped croquetas also impress if you need a pre-sandwich bite.

name: Fonda Balam
review: Is that the best lengua taco you’ve ever had? Is there a better birria in the city? You might find yourself asking a lot of questions at this casual fonda where it’s impossible not to over-order. What started out as a summer birria pop-up by celebrity chef Matty Matheson and former Quetzal chefs Kate Chomyshyn and Julio Guajardo quickly evolved into this brick-and-mortar where tortillas are made in-house. The menu has expanded sensibly with aguachile de camaron, spicy seafood cocktail and sweets like chocolate cake with coconut flan. This is food you crave on a regular basis served in an easy-going setting that doesn’t care how you’re dressed. Low-flung counter seats, sunshine-yellow napkins and cacti in every corner add to the charm.

name: SumiLicious Smoked Meat & Deli
review: In a non-descript Scarborough shopping center, Sumith Fernando’s smoked meat is something of a rite of passage. Fernando spent nearly two decades learning his craft at Schwartz's in Montreal before settling on his own recipe. His halal brisket is marinated in a secret spice blend for days, smoked for hours until tender and finally finished in a steamer. He opened in 2018 and has been behind the counter ever since, building sandwiches out of thinly sliced, peppery brisket piled high on soft, spongy rye smeared with yellow mustard. Against the advice of any physician, complete your order at this no-frills deli with poutine—fries topped with Quebec cheese curds and submerged in gravy. Ask for extra napkins, you'll need them.

name: Cherry Street Bar-B-Que
review: With views of the downtown skyline and construction sites on all sides, this popular Port Lands joint feels far from the rest of the city. In a way, it is. Pitmaster Lawrence La Pianta brings the barbecue traditions of the American South to Hogtown in this 1920s brick building that was once home to a bank. After years of competing and judging with the Kansas City Barbeque Society circuit, he knows his way around a broad range of tastes ranging from Texas-style brisket to St. Louis-style ribs. Lightly charred wings and snappy, finely spiced sausage links are sleeper hits. Everything is smoked on the patio inside of a redesigned shipping container and saucing is kept to a minimum. Stopping by on a weekend? Know that meats are prone to sell out.

name: Indian Street Food Company
review: Found in Leaside along a packed row of shops on Bayview Avenue, this neighborhood stalwart delivers a tight menu of street food favorites and regional curries from various corners of India. The dining room is wrapped in reclaimed wood panels and colorful murals, and cushy tables with white cloth invite further lingering. Over-ordering is easy, but friendly servers are quick to offer guidance. Deep-fried cauliflower finished in a sweet chili glaze is a kitchen specialty, but savory chaats, arriving lashed in refreshing chutneys, are worth an order. Order the thalis to see the breadth of this kitchen’s talent in one large, oversized platter featuring delicately spiced lamb curry, rich dhal makhani and a superb south Indian vegetable curry.

name: Café Caron
review: This cosy bistro is run by Alain Caron (a well-known TV personality and chef) and his family. The ambience here is typically French, as is the menu which features traditional, generous bistro-style dishes which are a work of art in their own right. Trying out the à la carte here is a real joy.

name: DiVino
review: This former school has been transformed into a warm, urban restaurant, including a graffiti portrait of Don Corleone! You can see the chefs working their magic in the open kitchen, where they create French and Mediterranean dishes full of creativity and nuanced flavours. Make sure you ask for advice when making your choice in the beautiful wine library.

name: Het Oude Gemeentehuis
review: Despite its name (‘the old town hall’) there is nothing old-fashioned about this restaurant, whose original features provide a striking contrast with the modern design and warm shades. Niels Minkman and Janneke Eerbeek are now at the helm and they have a stated policy of creating affordable modern dishes based on the freshest produce.

name: De Beejekurf
review: Mathijs Jacobs is a truly ambitious chef. If he’s brought a deer by a local huntsman or freshly harvested vegetables by a local farmer, his eyes light up. Whether he decides to cook his ingredients in a salt crust, grill them on the barbecue or use them in an ice-cream, he never lacks in inspiration and the result is always delicious!

name: Asian Glories
review: The Peking duck that you see hanging in the kitchen are one of the highlights on the attractive menu at this restaurant, while the pancakes that accompany the dish are prepared in front of you. The culinary traditions of Canton and Szechuan are to the fore here, served in elegant yet unfussy dishes which are full of generous flavours. A real feast!

name: Uit de Kunst
review: Hikers and cyclists who test themselves to their limits on the Vijlenberg are rewarded by this modern restaurant situated right at the top. The superb view from the terrace is a feast for the eyes, while the traditional dishes served here are a treat for the taste buds. Simple yet refined and delicious cuisine.

name: Bergpaviljoen
review: Whether you opt for the superb set menu offering a choice of dishes, more classic recipes and plates perfect for sharing on the à la carte, or fresh fish straight from the display counter, the choice is not an easy one in this bright restaurant featuring eye-catching Art Deco details and an extensive terrace. And whether you decide on ceviche or a cooked salmon fillet, the chef here complements his classical training with original ideas and superb flavours.

name: Huson
review: Huson is a trendy establishment where a lively industriousness always prevails. Here guests' mouths will water at the marvellous pairing of creativity with international ingredients in small dishes which are as subtle as they are exuberant. The chef is a dab hand at beautifully balancing fullness of flavour with freshness, as his signature dishes show.

name: Vineum
review: The wine list is the heart and soul of this warm, aptly named restaurant with an intimate urban garden to the rear. Owner David van Steenderen is a top sommelier who is constantly discovering new wines, while the same quality is mirrored in the cuisine, which features attractively presented dishes full of flavour. Classic cuisine, original ideas and real expertise act as the perfect complement to the fine wines.

name: Gym & Gin
review: The vintage colours and designer furniture in this open-plan restaurant give it a vibrant, funky ambience – the perfect setting for its exciting gin and cocktail menu and Kevin Valkhoff’s cuisine, which is full of subtle Asian influences and original flavours. The name Gym & Gin is a reference to the balance we all have to find between pleasure and healthy living – the choice is yours!

name: Brasserie van Baerle
review: There is no getting around it: wine is part of the core business of this elegant, ever-inviting luxury brasserie. The impressive selection of wines by the glass and extensive drinks menu will impress even the most seasoned connoisseur. Classics from the brasserie repertoire are served up here with great attention to detail and a sense of generosity. The steak tartare is a real crowd pleaser.

name: Umami by Han
review: If you find it difficult to decide what to eat, then you will enjoy the shared dining concept in this modern Asian restaurant. It boasts an impressive selection of dishes at very good value. Each course consists of 2 small dishes prepared in Japanese, Chinese, Thai, Indonesian or Vietnamese fashion, with a Western twist.

name: Plantage 87
cuisine: Modern Cuisine, Cuisine from the Marches
review: Plantage 87 has a phenomenal view of the surrounding marina. The chef has a 300m2 vegetable garden not far from the restaurant and he enjoys using a modern and creative approach to preparing vegetables. Top-quality main dishes accompanied by equally impressive garnishes which are prepared using the best of the home-grown produce.

name: Bistro de Olliemölle
review: This charmingly old-fashioned bistro, set in an old watermill, is a remarkable place. The water wheel still turns occasionally but the real treat is the idyllic terrace next to the water! Cooking is, in the main, traditional and generous, but you can also find some more contemporary dishes which demonstrate the chef’s experience.

name: Hofstede de Blaak
review: The charm of this authentic English country house (1907), the classic half-timbering and elegant details, the peaceful surroundings – it is hard not to be moved by this setting. The chef loves working with fine ingredients and accentuates their finesse with contemporary seasonings. He is fond of combining diverse flavours to create elegant nuances. Be sure to try the excellent set menu.

name: Kasteel Elsloo
review: Dining in a castle makes for a special experience. The surrounding natural beauty and centuries-old arcades beneath which guests take their seats cannot fail to impress. This fabulous setting inspires the chef to work with respect for the region, the seasons and sustainability. French and Mediterranean flavours dominate the appealingly updated menu, which now features occasionally innovative dishes. Wine lovers will delight in the enticing selection of wines sold by the glass.

name: Witlof
review: With the view of the River Waal, the jovial hostess and the chef who you see cooking as you make your way to use the facilities, at the Witlof, you will immediately feel at home. Jurgen Eikholt lovingly prepares classic cuisine with his trademark sophisticated, often oriental touches. Each dish on the menu can be ordered as a large or small portion.

name: Héron
review: From the farmer, to the gardener, to the fisherman, Héron's suppliers are all local. The season and the Dutch soil will determine what appears on the menu. Sustainability is key at this lively establishment, so dishes might feature previously unheard-of cuts of meat, a variety of preserves and foraged ingredients, and your dessert could contain fish garum. The chef will surprise you with his novel ways of putting local produce centre stage.

name: Bistrobar Berlin
review: This vibrant bistro-bar shares its avant-garde spirit with Berlin. Choose a spot in which to enjoy the restaurant’s home-grown creativity: the music is louder downstairs, while upstairs you’ll find more comfort. The cooking is modern and daring and the menu is international and eclectic – don’t miss the Kreuzberg dumplings with frankfurter sausage!

name: Hoog Holten
review: Your experience at Hoog Holten begins with the drive there: the charm of the surrounding Salland countryside is captivating in itself. The terrace of this romantic establishment, housed in an old hunting lodge, happens to be one of the most beautiful in the country! Brasserie Birds keeps things traditional – go to the restaurant for more varied, contemporary cuisine. The set menu changes daily, but always seeks inspiration abroad for its sometimes truly innovative dishes.

name: De Watermolen
review: The watermill dating back to 1391 is the main attraction of this rustic restaurant, although of course the warmth of the place and lively terrace are also a draw. The chef sometimes opts for more modern techniques, but mainly serves honest, traditional dishes. Vegetarians always have good options here, including the set menu.

name: Élevé
review: A superlative view from the top of the WTC Hotel over Leeuwarden is underscored by a hip, casually welcoming ambience. The restaurant is both affordable and yet exclusive. Chef Kalkman’s cooking is modern, subtle and free of unnecessary frills. You can expect premium local produce, jazzed up with the occasional modern twist and generous flavours.

name: De Watergeus
review: The walk alongside the canals affords a foretaste of what you can expect in this refurbished restaurant that enjoys a superb waterside location. The chef mixes classical recipes with generosity and modern textures. His culinary palette is diverse and intriguing and the formula is highly recommended. Enquire about overnight stays and boat trips (with a picnic basket) on the Nieuwkoopse Plassen.

name: Oogst
review: Oogst's warm vibe fits the cosy Buurtschap centrum 2005 like a glove. There is something of the lively Parisian bistro about this establishment, which makes it all the more enjoyable to dine here. The set menu is always determined by what the Laantje Voorham vegetable garden has to offer. The versatility of vegetables and herbs provides subtle nuances. Chef Van Bommel's modern and always generous creations are fragrant with punchy flavours. Plus, it's great value for money!

name: Promessa
review: “Food is art” is the motto of this relaxed restaurant, a mantra that is evident both in the trendy decor and on the plate. Aesthetics are key here yet without neglecting flavour, with impressive creativity and a variety of influences forming the basis for cuisine that is full of unique character. The varied choice of dishes will rouse immediate interest and ensure that you won’t leave disappointed!

name: A-Fusion
review: This intimate restaurant will entice you with its array of Chinese, Japanese, Thai and Korean dishes. On entering, you will see sushi being made to order, and as you go further in you will notice the barbecue and the dim sum and wok kitchen. Thanks to the reasonably priced à la carte menu and small dishes, you can try everything. Deep flavours, spices, umami, super fresh fish... a real gem of Asian cuisine!

name: Diverso
review: On the order form, tick a choice of one of the five dishes from each course, and prepare for a meal full of southern sunshine. The 5-course meal is superb - and so is the menu! The typically Mediterranean dishes are as strong and tasty as the menu is diverse, offering a southern European feast to be enjoyed in an attractive cosy ambience.

name: Rust Wat
review: After exploring the region, take a seat on the waterside terrace surrounded by forest and admire a scene worthy of an Impressionist work of art. Pleasure is the watchword in this cosy inn. The (generous) entremets provide a glimpse of the culinary scope, side by side more modern creations. The chef’s enthusiasm can be tasted in bang-on food depicted by gutsy flavours and free of fripperies.

name: De Houtloods
review: This old woodshed (1867) has retained its industrial character while combining it with modern comforts. The menu is clear and straightforward, offering guests a choice of fresh, spicy, rich or sweet dishes. The surprise lies in the intense flavours of each dish, with the occasional Asian twist, and the way the ingredients are prepared. The restaurant’s food bar, De Wagon, has the same creative feel.

name: Bistro
review: This charming bistro occupies the front room of the farm that is also home to its older Michelin-starred sibling De Gieser Wildeman. The cuisine and name are perfectly matched: traditional, generous and quite simply delicious. One of the highlights on the menu is the crispy duck leg with cabbage. The attractive prices here are as tempting as the cooking!

name: Tapisco
review: For centuries this was a famous bookshop; today this restaurant full of character and with a Mediterranean flair is regarded as the place to go for Spanish tapas and Portuguese petiscos. The experienced chef creates small typical dishes prepared with quality produce, not too complex but full of flavour, that take guests on an incredible Mediterranean journey.

name: Le Nord
review: This authentic farmhouse dating from 1885 boasts plenty of rural charm and modern comfort. The finesse with which the French chef pays tribute to his homeland is a testament to his expertise. More modern inspirations add nuance and a dash of excitement. Try the tuna pizza on the (tempting) menu, created in honour of his mentor Joop Braakhekke.

name: Pouwe
review: Vintage colours give this modern lounge-style restaurant a pleasant feel, while the large open-plan kitchen immediately attracts attention. Full of passion for their work, the Pouwe couple have created an attractive restaurant with a youthful feel. The chef combines flavours from different countries in his cuisine, adding a creative twist that gives his dishes an extra punch.

name: Hof van Herstal
review: Hof van Herstal is an elegant restaurant with a decor that does full justice to its rich history. This establishment has bags of character. Chef Martin Bruggeman takes great pride in his work, proving every day that he is a true master of his trade. He slaughters his own game (venison is a must here!) and is happy to make judicious wine recommendations. His generous sauces are the best evidence of his culinary skill.

name: Publique
review: The corner building where vintage and contemporary design merge with beautiful stained-glass windows is the place to be. This relaxed little place is popular with locals, who come for the market-fresh cuisine. Chef Plat gives vegetables (extensive vegetable menu available) pride of place in fresh dishes which he likes to give a Mediterranean twist. His choices are sometimes rather daring, but always hit the mark, like the amazing shallot and white wine vinaigrette with sweet/salty sea urchin he serves to accompany monkfish.

name: De Lindeboom New Style
review: De Lindeboom boasts plenty of style both in terms of the charm of the building (1760), its typical Limburg hospitality, and its varied menu. Chef Jan-Willem demonstrates his preference for Mediterranean freshness and international inspiration on a menu ranging from traditional sole to vegetarian dishes, bringing together all the ingredients needed to delight his guests.

name: Umami by Han
review: Renowned chef Han Ji has created a recipe for success at Umami, a bright, contemporary restaurant in which he concocts high-flying Asian fusion cuisine. The range of tasting sensations is suitably impressive, ranging from sweet to savoury and crunchy and smooth in intense dishes full of flavour and colour. An irresistibly exotic experience!

name: Sukade
review: The succade – candied citrus peel – that was once sold in this warehouse dating back to 1860 has now been replaced by exciting, imaginative dishes created by a chef who focuses especially on fruit and vegetables. The attention to greens in the enticing vegetable menu is an additional plus, as is the delightful terrace overlooking the water. Delicious food served all day.

name: Herberg Stadt Stevenswaert
review: Marcus Schmidt’s inn sits on a picturesque tree-lined square, at the centre of an island flanked by a canal and the River Maas. The menu changes frequently, with seasonal produce – including vegetables from their garden – harmoniously coming together in creative dishes; the desserts in particular are delicious. The restaurant also offers a great selection of German wines.

name: De Uitkijk
review: With its magnificent natural setting, a lavender-filled terrace with a southern feel, and a restaurant with a country estate atmosphere, De Uitkijk offers a winning combination. Guests can watch the seasons change on the plate, with herbs from the chef's own garden. The elaborate dishes here are full of fresh flavour and boast lots of variety.

name: L'Auberge de Neercanne
review: This restaurant, which now has a stylish new look, boasts a unique setting under the vaults of the old chapel at Château Neercanne. Take a seat on the stunning outdoor terrace and enjoy classic dishes reinterpreted with a modern twist by the chef, who likes to use produce grown in his own garden in his cuisine.

name: Chef aan de Werf
review: Enjoy a local beer as an aperitif before discovering Charly de Wijs' selection of international dishes, which feature local, subtly flavoured and sustainably sourced ingredients and draw on inspirations from around the globe. His winning combinations include options such as harissa with a fillet of fish, flatbread with carrots, tahini and feta. Just bear in mind that the chef serves up very generous portions! Housed in an old industrial building, this lively restaurant with its vintage decor is bound to have you coming back for more.

name: Tabkeaw
review: With its bamboo panelling, “pagoda” bar and typical landscapes on the walls, Tabkeaw’s interior is a journey in itself, with the lively buzz of the Wyck district providing the backdrop. The cuisine here is as traditional as the decor, featuring the authentic aromas of a tom kha kai, and the spicy harmony of fresh fish, curry and coconut. A culinary adventure!

name: Bovenmeester
review: The head teacher left this former school building some time ago, and although the coat hooks are still in place, the decor has been pleasantly renovated. The result is a warm atmosphere complemented by a cosy lounge area. The menu is seasonal, and the excellent multi-choice option offers quality cuisine at affordable prices.

name: Harry's
review: This luxury brasserie is as cosmopolitan as it is vibrant. French flair characterises both the ambience and the cuisine. On the menu, international flavours and vegetarian options show that the chefs are keeping up with the times, but not at the expense of the golden rules of superior brasserie cuisine. The kitchen garden is a manifestation of their sustainable approach (more details on the website). Creative, local, seasonal: Harry's ticks all the boxes!

name: La Mère Anne
review: La Mère Anne is a huge business encompassing a range of activities. You can hire the venue for parties, spend the night in modern guestrooms, but above all, enjoy good food! The chef favours regional produce, which he showcases in contemporary dishes. These steer clear of frills, focusing instead on straightforward, delicious flavours. The restaurant will be closed from 27 December 2022 until mid-March 2023 because of renovation works.

name: Zilt & Zoet
review: The refreshed interior of this countryside villa combines the modern and the vintage, and is a great example of cosy Dutch ambience. The extensive set menu (a choice of three, four or five courses) is impressive. It is created by a chef who creates modern, lavish dishes from largely seasonal produce.

name: Spandershoeve
review: Spandershoeve has been showcasing traditional Indonesian cuisine since 1972. Here, Anita watches over her grandson Timo, ensuring that authentic flavours are still to the fore, despite the chef’s eye for new trends – for example, he flavours his different dishes with his own special mixture of spices. An excellent choice for anyone wishing to experience true Indonesian hospitality.

name: Mijn Streek
review: After a visit to the Schunck Museum, make sure you go to the fifth floor of the Glass Palace. This cosy brasserie takes you on an international adventure. The dishes, served in starter-sized portions, include Middle Eastern flavours and vegetarian options, and there is an emphasis on vegetables and avoiding food waste... Straightforward, authentic cuisine with intense flavours.

name: LEV Foodbar
review: The relaxed atmosphere at LEV perfectly matches the concept behind this food bar: sharing dishes and enjoying good food together. The dishes (in snack-sized portions) are not overcomplicated; a couple of ingredients suffice to create amazing taste sensations. Steak tartare, pork tenderloin, cauliflower tempura, truffle risotto... At LEV, the table quickly fills with irresistible delicacies, often prepared using produce from the Achterhoek region. The perfect accompaniment to one of the many beers!

name: Raedthuys
review: Just about everything is homemade in this restaurant, which has its own bakery, own patisserie and even its own smokehouse! Choose from the wide selection of generous dishes created by chef Marion, who focuses on genuine traditional flavours with no unnecessary frills. Combine your classic meal with one of the numerous beers on offer here, many of which are on tap.

name: De Beleving
review: This convivial brasserie boasts all the attractions that you come to expect from a true Bib Gourmand address: a varied choice of enticing yet unfussy dishes that are generous and tasty. The chef does allow himself a few modern touches in his textures, although his cuisine is firmly focused on top-quality traditional ingredients such as haddock and Iberico pork presa. A splendid experience!

name: Gastrobar Ster
review: Terry Priem is a man with two faces – on the one hand, he’s the graphic artist (aka Ster) who, using aerosol paints, decorated the dining room; on the other, he’s a chef who demonstrates his artistic creativity in bold dishes which add subtle innovations to classic favourites. Original cocktails and excellent wines complete the picture.

name: Bij Mette
review: Picturesque Linschoten is worth a visit in its own right, but be sure to look out for this beautifully converted grocery shop with its distinctive spiral staircase located a stone's throw from the leaning clock tower. This is old Dutch charm at its best! Chef-patron Carel Alberts welcomes you personally before showing off his expertise in the French classics. Wonderful local produce, intense sauces, respect for tradition: it all makes for an enjoyable culinary experience. Feel free to ask the chef about his French wine list – he will be happy to tell you more.

name: Red Orchids
review: If you have a hard time making decisions, we suggest you head to this intimate, trendy restaurant where the menu brings together Japanese, Chinese, Thai and Indonesian specialities. The chef always manages to add just the right dose of spices, creating dishes full of rich flavours and crisp textures. Subtle Asian cuisine at reasonable prices.

name: Herberg de Witte Gans
review: This rustic restaurant is a favourite pit stop for walkers, cyclists and food lovers. The terrace is one of its main draws ; another is the superb Bib Gourmand-awarded menu, which features local produce, nods to the East, and vegetarian options. The creative chef works his ingredients hard and prides himself on the presentation of his dishes.

name: Coperto Restobar
review: Marble tables, luxurious bucket seats and the use of glass all add to the chic ambience in this restaurant. The concept is as hip as the location – you’re spoilt for choice here, as the menu features a superb selection of modern dishes combining subtle textures, international influences and local flavours. The reasonably priced wine list adds to the appeal.

name: Bistro TWO
review: How about a drink at the Dux hotel’s rooftop bar with its view of the town, lunch on the waterfront terrace or dinner in the chic, lively bistro? TWO is one of Roermond’s must-visit venues, offering a fascinating choice between typical bistro dishes such as duck liver terrine and more modern options such as meat loaf cooked in cocoa. Distinctive, updated cuisine which is quite simply delicious!

name: Het Oude Dykhuys
review: This elegant dike house with an attractive location right on the water’s edge provides a delightful dining experience, thanks to its generous traditional cuisine, attentive service and excellent wines from the cellar. The chef adds the occasional contemporary touch to his cuisine, while staying faithful to the flavours of bygone days.

name: Groenewoud
review: A few authentic decorative features remind us that despite its comfortable and even trendy feel we are in one of the oldest cafés in Nijmegen. The experienced chef at the helm conjures up generous French cuisine with the occasional subtle and surprising touch. Dishes cooked to perfection, a mastery of acidic flavours, intense sauces, plus excellent value for money!

name: Alma Bodega
review: Situated on the ground floor, the more informal and relaxed sibling to Alma boasts a chic marble decor. The menu offers a whole host of tempting dishes which are cosmopolitan and generous in style, including updated classics which immediately catch the eye. Excellent wine list. Don’t forget to book in advance!

name: Klaas
review: Take two talented friends with experience working in a number of top-end establishments and the result is this friendly restaurant. Klaas serves well-known classics with an original twist, resulting in dishes which are full of fun, delicate and exciting flavours. The restaurant’s selection of regional beers and gins is equally impressive, including Witte Klaas, their quality Witbier.

name: Domenica
review: Domenica’s outdoor terrace is the ideal place to sit and enjoy the lively atmosphere of the Jordaan district. This restaurant is popular with locals, who come here for the Mediterranean cuisine heavily influenced by Italy, featuring dishes such as traditional linguini with a delicious sauce or the restaurant’s own take on ceviche, all bursting with flavour. The owner has a real passion for wine, which he happily shares with guests.

name: Suzie's en Van Aken
review: Committed to sustainability (nose-to-tail eating, fermentation etc), Chef Tom draws on the latest culinary techniques to create exciting, colourful dishes full of finesse and imagination, inspired by his travels, especially to Asia. The jovial Suzanne plays her part, serving up excellent wine and dessert recommendations. The natural vibe of this cosy establishment will make your dinner that little bit more enjoyable.

name: Arles
review: This attractive bistro brings a touch of Provence to Amsterdam, with framed photos of the chef's native city Arles adorning the walls. The chef, a fan of jazz music, creates neo-bistro-style dishes which offer a fresh reinterpretation of familiar French flavours. The fixed-price menu, which changes every month, is a real winner!

name: La Vie
review: The 'living room' of the Hotel Valuas is a cosy luxury brasserie that is open all day long. Generous breakfasts, pastries or afternoon snacks, an enticing à la carte menu and a three-course set menu... there's something for everyone. The chef takes his inspiration from classic French cuisine and selects high-quality (often local) ingredients – and it's outstanding value for money. A seat on the terrace, overlooking the River Meuse, is a must!

name: Auberge Jean & Marie
review: Whether you choose to go to the back of the restaurant to select your own bottle from the wine cellar or you ask Jan and Marije for their exceptional advice, you’ll be spoilt for choice in this delightfully informal restaurant which is perfect for wine lovers. Rich and tasty traditional French cuisine with the occasional contemporary twist accompanies these fine wines.

name: Boompjes
cuisine: Country cooking, Cuisine from the Marches
review: The use of trees, plants and wood add a natural feel to the interior decor in this restaurant. Chef Volman is an ambassador for Dutch cuisine, giving produce grown in the vegetable garden a prominent place in his dishes. He likes to surprise his guests with the many different ways he prepares vegetables, offering an experience which showcases Dutch produce to the full!

name: Rijsel
review: The interior of this lively establishment resembles a classroom, and indeed this building was once a home economics school. Today you can see the 'master' at work preparing his lesson in French gastronomy thanks to the open kitchen. He has a sound knowledge of his ingredients and incorporates a nod to Flemish cuisine into his no-nonsense dishes. Whether you order the intensely flavoured typical Southern French fish soup or côte de bœuf served with a house-made béarnaise sauce and fried potatoes: at Rijsel, every dish is a feast!

name: Nova
review: Located on the edge of the Bergse Bos forest, and featuring a romantic terrace, a pontoon on the River Rotte and a cosy interior ambience, Nova is a delightful restaurant where chef Martin Vaandrager offers guests a menu with a varied choice. His contemporary cuisine is teeming with flavours, combining amusing ideas and impressive expertise in his dishes. A fine example of value for money… and pleasure!

name: De Schans by Mike & Wes
review: When they took over De Schans, Mike and Wes, respectively sommelier and chef, added a trendier, more relaxed vibe, whilst retaining the establishment’s commitment to fine food and wine. The chef crafts dishes in tune with the zeitgeist using cutting-edge culinary techniques to create a subtle blend of textures and unexpected flavours. The set menu is definitely worth sampling!

name: Basaal
review: A cosy neighbourhood restaurant, Scandinavian and vintage vibes included, nice terrace on the water: what a nice place Basaal is! The full à la carte offer and the attractive wine list complete the picture. The modern market cuisine is based on intense sauces, generous flavours and creative, tantalising ideas. A deliciously unconstrained feast of flavour!

name: De Grote Frederik Bistro
review: In this cosy local bistro you immediately get the feeling that guests always come first. This is typified by the excellent front-of-house hospitality of host Marjon, who is delighted to offer advice on a superb selection of wines to accompany chef Arnejan’s unique dishes, which are playful and unpretentious, yet which feature wonderful and surprising flavours.

name: Bistro LOF
review: The experienced chef at this modern yet rustic restaurant in an old farmhouse in Broekhuizen park takes inspiration from Dutch ingredients, including produce from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden. His dishes are simple yet full of intense modern flavours, which are rich, carefully thought out and painstakingly prepared. Even the simple tomato with prawns dish will surprise you!

name: Waers
review: Waers is the incarnation of anti-conformity, which sums up Dennis Vermeulen to a T! In his restaurant showcasing a strong sense of Scandinavian purity, he brings out the very best of market-fresh ingredients and the seasons. There’s no fuss here, just original, well-balanced dishes with a contemporary feel that are well worth discovering and offer excellent value for money.

name: Fa. Pekelhaaring
review: Welcome to the urban canteen of a number of Amsterdam’s local residents – a relaxed eatery without unnecessary sophistication, but one which is both authentic and welcoming. The cuisine is influenced (but not exclusively) by Italy and the chef enjoys adding his own variations and personal touches (such as crunchy textures and local influences) to his cooking. The varied à la carte is impressive indeed!

name: Blauw
review: Tradition, a “street food” influence, authenticity and purity are the words that best sum up this popular restaurant showcasing the full array of Indonesian cuisine. Its “rice table” provides an excellent opportunity to discover the talent that the chef employs in his seasonings and intense flavours. And don’t forget to order the delicious roasted goat meat!

name: Bistrôt Chapeau
review: Experience the charm of its colourful bistro decor, the peace and quiet of the terrace and a soothing ambience in this restaurant straight out of quintessential Burgundy! Here, Nicky Quarz revives often forgotten French classics without any unnecessary frivolity yet teeming with authentic flavours. Through his sauces, intensity etc, enjoy a welcome return to the very roots of French cuisine.

name: 't Nieuwe Diekhuus
review: This old thatch-roofed farm on the banks of the Yssel provides a charming setting (including a terrace with a stunning view of the river) in which you’ll feel immediately at ease. To this splendid backdrop, enjoy international delicacies (often with an Asian influence) prepared with top-quality ingredients and well-crafted garnishes that provide the perfect accompaniment. Generous cuisine that is well thought out yet gentle on the pocket!

name: Restaurant ñ
review: The yellow façade of this relaxed restaurant gives it a southern feel, which is further enhanced by the aromas of typical, authentic Spanish and Mediterranean dishes that greet you as you step through the door. The delicious options on the menu include fresh seafood, spicy chilli peppers, and dishes served with fresh, sophisticated sauces, as well as an excellent selection of cheese and charcuterie.

name: Moustique
review: This highly modern restaurant in the centre of Haarlem is open almost every day. Here, you’ll find an extensive menu on which the chef showcases his experience through cuisine with an Asian inspiration and modern presentation, including a choice of vegetarian dishes and plenty of intense and authentic flavours. An impressive new arrival on the city’s food scene!

name: Oriole
review: Oriole is a peaceful haven amid the hustle and bustle of the city centre. The decor in this luxurious brasserie is truly splendid (especially the stunning bar), but a table on the terrace is a real must. This hidden treasure offers a contemporary version of Mediterranean flavours (with particular attention paid to vegetables), that matches the setting perfectly. Purity, finesse and passion combine here to create a festival of southern flavours.

name: Fellin
review: You’re guaranteed a warm welcome at this café-cum-bistro set within a red brick building on the edge of the Old Town. It has something of a bohemian air, courtesy of a tiled bar, a mix of artwork and a laid-back vibe. Carefully prepared, traditional European dishes burst with freshness and flavour.

name: Origines
review: A narrow lane near the main square leads to this endearing restaurant whose rear patio features an olive tree in its centre. Chef Céline finds her inspiration in seasonal market ingredients, which form the backbone of her mouth-watering menu. Modern, complex-free dishes of Gallic origins, underscored by feminine delicacy and exquisite, distinctive flavours.

name: Maïnoï
review: Whilst refreshingly modern, Maïnoï has not ditched its traditions. Decorative Thai details are combined with bare wood panelling to create a warm interior. The seasoned chef combines exuberant familiar flavours and cannot be rivalled for his way with sauces. Each dish is a culinary masterpiece, particularly when jazzed up with the chef’s creative flair. The menu is bold and daring and pleasant surprises await the diner.

name: Tapa Ti
review: A generous array of flavoursome cured meats, a ceviche of seabass in tiger’s milk, followed by a succulent cut of meat or a platter of seafood? The family-run Tapa Ti shines a ray of Spanish sunshine on Sterrebeek. Relaxed and contemporary vibe. Don’t expect a run-of-the-mill tapas bar, however, as the chef adds Asian notes to his varied tapas menu. Ideal for a festive occasion with family and friends.

name: Fleur de Sel
review: Self-taught chefs Slava and Antoine have set up their friendly establishment two steps from the French border. The irresistible duo bowls us over – his passion and food-wine pairings and her delicate, generous cooking. Slava’s meticulous attention to detail results in balanced dishes that combine fresh, acidic, spicy and a host of other delicious flavours. The ingredient takes pride of place in each carefully thought-out dish.

name: Les Potes au Feu
review: A couple of pals, Damien Gorjanec and François Schepens, are at the helm of this casual establishment. They have pooled their respective experiences into a menu that throbs with choice. The local vegetables literally shine in the plate. Never OTT, the focus is on finding interesting combinations that harmoniously blend unctuosity, crunchiness, freshness and intensity.

name: Table Rase
review: Ludovic and Clarisse set out first and foremost to offer diners a good meal. Starting with the eater-friendly prices of this pleasant establishment. Chef Ludovic is keen to work with local produce and each dish displays his culinary expertise, enhanced with acidic, savoury or other subtle touches. The regularly renewed formula menu is highly recommended.

name: Nr.12 by Helsen
review: In addition to being the most fashionable restaurant on Herentals’ main square, N°12 is also the most delicious. Veteran chef Frédéric Helsen is a dab hand at rustling up dishes to share (of which we wager you will order too many, so vast is the choice!). He chooses to reinterpret culinary classics in an amusing, no-frills, highly individual manner to the delight of our tastebuds.

name: Les Terrasses de l'Our
review: The opportunity to dine on the riverside terrace of this restaurant is not to be missed. Natural materials adorn the interior of this endearing brasserie, which is emblematic of the Ardennes, as is the food: game, trout, local ham prepared to textbook perfection… A daring new spin jazzes up familiar favourites, always with lashings of fresh flavour.

name: Cœur de Bœuf
review: The grill gets ample use in this family-run brasserie, a genuine Bib Gourmand. Traditional meat dishes and ancient recipes such as sautéed calf’s brains are generously prepared with great delicacy and the respect for authentic whole-hearted flavours. Don’t hesitate to take the menu home – you’re in a for a host of amusing surprises!

name: Au Tour du Vin
review: While wine may not be the only ingredient on the menu, it is clearly a prominent feature of this pleasantly lively bistro. The chef amply demonstrates his mastery of French cuisine, treating himself to the luxury of more personal interpretations from time to time. We also recommend the next - door ice cream parlour.

name: l'Epicurien
review: Sébastien Brela is a true food lover. His passion for fine ingredients is obvious as soon as you peruse the menu. Distinctive flavours play a central role, while generous sauces add a punchy twist. Unexpected associations and textures create a genuine surprise. The fixed-price menus demonstrate that it is possible to be a gourmet food lover without breaking the bank!

name: InVINcible
review: Take a seat at the counter and admire the chefs weaving their culinary magic as you peruse the knock-out wine list. Next, chef Burssens will demonstrate why French cuisine continues to enjoy such a stellar reputation – a truly invincible combination. Despite the relatively concise menu, it’s really difficult to make your choice from the range of generous dishes and subtle yet distinctive flavours.

name: Felicità
review: Calabrian ham, olive oil from Campania and Lombardy mustard are among the premium delicacies you can expect to sample. The cheerful owner loves telling tales about his travels to find these culinary gems and ancient recipes. Wholesome Italian food made with first-rate ingredients. Traditional pasta oozing with character and aromas. Yummy!

name: Biestro H-eat
review: A hip bistro that never fails to appeal. Trendy lighting, a vintage wood-burning stove and a full view of the chefs consummately rustling up flavoursome fare in the open kitchen. Their boundless inspiration features Flemish classics, Asian nuances and Mediterranean flair in a scrumptious menu. The epitome of a friendly bistro – from the décor to the plate!

name: Le Tournant
review: The chef of this neighbourhood restaurant was a movie producer in a former life and his cinematographic flair is clearly visible in the restaurant’s friendly interior. The stage is set for a varied wine list and authentic bistro fare that will suit all tastes. The slow cooked meat dishes are, however, what top the bill.

name: Gaston Vouzote
review: If you feel like a slap-up meal with all the trimmings, make a beeline for this authentic brasserie whose vintage interior is paired with a Parisian vibe. Family favourites that warm the soul, such as traditional terrine (depending on the season), steak tartare and soufflé, set the scene on the menu. Homemade, hearty cooking and a festival of flavours. Gaston Vouzoute knows how to satisfy our appetites and our senses!

name: Borse van Amsterdam
review: Borse is a landmark of Amsterdam, as much for its colossal architecture and historic Flemish décor as for its restaurant. With its huge terrace overlooking the Grand-Place, it has been a blue-chip value for donkey’s years. The menu focuses on generous helpings of time-honoured family favourites and you will instantly be able to taste the deft hand of a seasoned chef who knows how to enhance authentic flavours.

name: De Farmasie
review: A good meal is just what the doctor ordered! So, book a table quickly in this fashionable establishment, quirkily adorned with a 17C pharmacy cabinet. The chef, a keen “farm to table” adept who is equally at home with rib steak and Thai curry, demonstrates an innate flair for flavours and tastes. The owner adores sharing his love of fine (Italian) wine with diners.

name: Les Fines Gueules
review: This bright, airy restaurant is surrounded by the gently undulating green landscapes of the Herve region. Home to an inventive chef, it offers a tempting à la carte selection, as well as a simpler set menu. The chef puts a great deal of effort into his dishes, playing with techniques and combinations without compromising on flavour and generosity.

name: La Fermette des Pins
review: A picturesque farmstead in the heart of the countryside whose terrace makes the most of this idyllic rural setting – ideal to sample top-notch brasserie fare. You won’t regret booking a table here! The seasoned chef’s veal kidneys served with a velvety béarnaise sauce are out of this world. In short: the quintessence of wholesome country cooking.

name: Olijfboom
review: Highly polished silverware, a fantastic collection of bottles and knickknacks set the quirky, antique dealer interior of Olijfboom, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the chef is a keen collector of vintage chinaware. However, his main talent is regaling us with old-school cooking. In keeping with tradition, he unfussily enhances the ingredient which he serves generously, focusing on the flavour. An impressive wine list completes this fine dining experience.

name: Brasserie de l'Expo
review: If you’re looking for a characteristic Brussels brasserie, take a seat on the lovely terrace or in the dining room, whose red colour scheme is dotted with Art deco and 1958 Expo details. Slick service by waiters in bow ties. The patriotic line-up of Belgian classics includes cheese fritters, américain (beef tartare in lashings of mayo) and French fries, oysters and mussels in season. The epitome of generosity!

name: Amu
review: The elegant, intimate decor of Amu sports a marriage of romantic and sexy. In her open kitchen, Marjanne Moonen rustles up genuine delicacies with just a few ingredients that are free of fancy frills, but always spot on. Her distinctive culinary signature is a patchwork of Mediterranean influences, spices and fermentation techniques. The wine list is sourced from all over the world.

name: Chermanne
review: Veteran chef, Stéphane Chermanne, grows his own vegetables so he knows how to coax and nurture their individual flavours to the full. He is also keen on working with less popular cuts of meat, adding Mediterranean touches to his recipes. Heart-warming food that hits the spot every time served in a tastefully appointed contemporary interior.

name: Le Grand Maur
review: An air of romantic nostalgia reigns throughout this charming small Ardennes castle. Ideally located for a spot of sight-seeing in Spa, the castle also serves a bang-up meal. The attractive range of dishes demonstrates the chef’s passion for first-class produce, which he prepares generously, flanked by polished side dishes and subtle sauces.

name: dis-moi où ?
review: Tell me where? Well, here! If you are looking for food that combines fresh ingredients, tradition and generosity, this is the place for you. This spruce restaurant is heaven for food lovers. Chef Michiels not only knows how to concoct good sauces and grilled meat but he is a dab hand at whipping up more elaborate fare of great delicacy. Choosing from the extensive menu will pose something of a conundrum. Why not try one of the excellent whiskeys at the end of your meal?

name: L'Entre D'Eux
review: Caroline Druine combines delicacy and generosity in dishes that demonstrate her commitment to local, organic ingredients. For example, she pairs wild boar from the next-door forest with “grandma’s” red cabbage and a gutsy dark brown cocoa sauce that is so good you will be licking your fingers after mopping it up with bread! The casual vibe is further amplified by Alexandre’s natural, friendly service. A small patio in the garden planted with pear trees is ideal for alfresco summer dining.

name: Des Ardennes
review: The Maqua family’s charming hotel has been welcoming guests in the Ardennes since 1900 and several generations continue to work in the family establishment. The peaceful rooms overlook the rolling countryside, while in the restaurant, the accent is on satisfying French favourites, albeit in keeping with today’s tastebuds. The cooking is spot on and flavoursome. Splendid wine cellar.

name: La Cantine du Châtelet
review: If you fancy sharing a plate of first-rate tapas in a trendy, casual vibe, turn left and head for the lounge. On your right lies the elegant restaurant which offers an enticing menu in the evenings. The chef combines his know-how of Belgian classics with ideas gleaned from numerous forays to Spain. One is inevitably won over by his communicative creativity. Vividly rendered, no frills food!

name: Kok Sur Mer
review: Established in a handsome villa-cum-cottage, Jean-Philippe Furnémont’s traditional know-how is in the masterclass category, illustrated by flawlessly cooked beef fillet, exquisite noisette butter served with North Sea sole or explosively fresh tartar of seabass. Each dish bears the signature of this audacious chef. The formula menu is rich in enticing discoveries.

name: Le Moulin
review: While on your getaway in the Ardennes be sure to knock on the door of this old mill. The welcome is warm, the setting cosy and the prices reasonable. The menu boasts up - to - the - minute flavours and an excellent lunch special. On the garden terrace you can hear the soothing sound of the river.

name: K restaurant
review: The imposing K gives you a choice of a modern setting, a more elegant, classical room and a terrace. The fantastic range of dishes is further proof that everyone will find something to suit their palate. From classical dishes and brasserie fare to more elaborate recipes, all prepared generously and, wherever possible, at the last minute. Go on! Treat your taste buds!

name: Den Duyventooren
review: The spruce, traditional façade of this ancestral farmstead hides a vibrant modern interior. The peaceful terrace is bliss on hot summer days. The establishment has acquired a faithful cohort of regulars, attracted by the set menus and Inge Herteleer’s enticing carte. Her seasonal cooking throbs with traditional generosity and is dotted with contemporary touches. The shrimp fritters are stuffed to the brim, while a subtle champagne sauce enhances pheasant. Searingly good food!

name: La Maison Thai
review: Sample a refined version of bourgeois Thai cuisine in this exotic establishment. The characteristic harmony of rice or noodles, ginger, sweet-sour spices and other Thai delicacies unfold generously on the palate. It is a pleasure to taste and mix these spicy dishes. In winter, the Thai fondue (bookings only) is extremely popular!

name: La Taperia
review: Peter Cambré has been cooking for professional cyclists and top (inter)national artists for many years. Now, everyone can sample his culinary craftsmanship in this welcoming restaurant. You will be enchanted by globetrotting Peter’s fascination for Spanish culture and tapas. All the food is authentic, from the Spanish aperitif to his talented retakes of wholesome Flemish classics.

name: Le Coq en Pâte
review: The Bacchetta family has been regaling diners since 1972 in their elegant establishment. You will taste the best of fine Italian fare. Chef Olivier is meticulous, and his subtle blends of flavours delight the palate. He finds his inspiration in Italian traditions, which he updates with a creative talent that combines visual flair and a love of contrasts.

name: Trattoria Bazalia
review: The Italian sibling of Hofke van Bazel is upstairs from the Michelin star establishment. Its romantic interior is perfect for a dinner for two, possibly alfresco on the patio overlooking a pretty church. Ingredients from Puglia take the limelight, but the chef also celebrates other regions of Italy. Just the ticket for an authentic vitello tonnato, ossobuco or tiramisu, prepared with Italian passion. Extensive menu (also veggie dishes).

name: Cadre Culinaire
review: In addition to hailing from Alsace, Grégory Baruthio avows a passion for pastries, as you will soon realise, and his Gugelhupf is truly second to none! Ever enthusiastic, the chef dons his apron to enhance ingredients that suit the modern palate without losing sight of high-precision cooking and traditional generosity. A welcoming establishment with eater friendly prices.

name: Cul de Poule
review: A colourful, cartoon-inspired chicken adorns this small bistro, but the real draw is Arnaud Molle. This seasoned chef lets his creativity run riot in regularly changing menus with a Gallic slant. His food is flavoursome, original and ideally suited to make the most of fresh produce. His flawlessly cooked pheasant served with a creamy Fine Champagne cognac sauce is to die for! The meat, from his parent’s butchery, is first class and the prices are truly eater friendly – what more can we say?

name: De Maurice à Olivier
review: Amusingly, you walk past Maurice’s newsagents before reaching the Parisian-inspired bistro of his son, Olivier. Gallic tradition permeates both the service and the food. Flawlessly cooked duck, served with generous side dishes and a powerful sauce. The epitome of fine French cuisine, flanked with a well-stocked wine cellar and a splendid choice of cigars and whiskeys to finish your meal.

name: Plat préféré
review: Are you a fan of fine Flemish fare and family bistro classics? If so, you can probably bet that your favourite dish will be on the menu here. Chef Gouwy bends over backwards to satisfy his guests and his heart - warming cuisine is a genuine treat for hungry diners. Disarmingly simple and wholesome.

name: L'Ôthentique
review: All that remains of the former farmstead are the old stone vaults, yet the land and its produce are at the centre of this establishment.
